sentences.zh: 列傳第五十八

translations.literal: Biographies, number fifty-eight
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 58

sentences.zh: 韓褒趙肅子軌張軌李彥郭彥梁昕皇甫璠子誕辛慶之族子昂王子直杜杲呂思禮徐招檀翥孟信宗懍劉璠子祥兄子行本柳遐子莊

translations.literal: Han Bao; Zhao Su, son Gui; Zhang Gui; Li Yan; Guo Yan; Liang Xin; Huang Fufan, son Dan; Xing Qingzhi, clansman Ang; Wang Zizhi; Du Gao; Lu Sili; Xu Zhao; Tan Zhu; Meng Xin; Zong Lin; Liu Fan, son Xiang, elder brother's son Xingben; Liu Xia, son Zhuang
translations.idiomatic: Han Bao; Zhao Su and his son Gui; Zhang Gui; Li Yan; Guo Yan; Liang Xin; Huang Fufan and his son Dan; Xing Qingzhi and his clansman Ang; Wang Zizhi; Du Gao; Lu Sili; Xu Zhao; Tan Zhu; Meng Xin; Zong Lin; Liu Fan, his son Xiang, and his brother's son Xingben; Liu Xia and his son Zhuang

sentences.zh: 韓褒，字弘業，潁川潁陽人也。

translations.literal: Han Bao, style name Hongye, was a native of Yingyang in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Bao, whose style name was Hongye, came from Yingyang in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 祖環，魏平涼郡守、安定郡公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huan was Wei prefect of Pingliang and Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huan had served as prefect of Pingliang under Wei and held the title Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 父演，恆州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yan was governor of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan was governor of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 褒少有志尚，好學而不守章句。

translations.literal: Bao in youth had lofty aims, loved learning yet did not cling to textual glosses.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Bao harbored high ambitions; he loved learning but refused to be bound by commentarial pedantry.

sentences.zh: 其師怪問之，對曰：「文字之間，常奉訓誘，至於商較異同，請從所好。」

translations.literal: His teacher, wondering, questioned him; he replied, "Between the written words I always receive your instruction; as for weighing agreements and differences, allow me to follow my own bent."
translations.idiomatic: When his teacher questioned this odd habit, he answered, "I always heed your guidance in reading the texts themselves; but when it comes to debating fine points of interpretation, let me follow my own inclinations."

sentences.zh: 師因此奇之。

translations.literal: The teacher for this reason regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His teacher marveled at this reply.

sentences.zh: 及長，涉獵經史，深沈有遠略。

translations.literal: When grown, he ranged through the classics and histories, deep and reserved, with far-reaching strategy.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he ranged widely through the classics and histories, and was known for his depth of mind and long-range vision.

sentences.zh: 屬魏室喪亂，避地夏州。

translations.literal: It happened that the Wei house fell into disorder; he fled to Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei court collapsed into chaos, he took refuge in Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 時周文帝為刺史，素聞其名，待以客禮。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wen of Zhou was regional inspector; having long heard his name, he received him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai was then regional inspector there; he had long heard of Bao's reputation and treated him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 及賀拔岳為侯莫陳悅所害，諸將遣使迎周文。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, the generals sent envoys to welcome Zhou Wen.
translations.idiomatic: After Heba Yue was murdered by Houmochen Yue, the commanders sent envoys to summon Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 周文問以去留之計，褒曰：「此天授也，何可疑乎！」

translations.literal: Zhou Wen asked him about plans to go or stay; Bao said, "This is Heaven's gift—what is there to doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai asked his advice on whether to accept the summons. Bao said, "This is a mandate from Heaven—why hesitate?"

sentences.zh: 周文納焉。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 及為丞相，引為錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor, he appointed him recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuwen Tai became chancellor, he appointed Bao recording secretary on his staff.

sentences.zh: 賜姓侯呂陵氏。

translations.literal: He was granted the surname Houluoling.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the surname Houluoling.

sentences.zh: 大統初，遷行台左丞，賜爵三水縣伯、丞相府從事中郎，出鎮淅、酈。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, he was transferred to left assistant of the executive agency, granted the title Baron of Sanshui, made attendant gentleman of the chancellor's office, and sent out to garrison Xi and Li.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era he was promoted to left assistant of the executive agency, ennobled as Baron of Sanshui, appointed attendant gentleman in the chancellor's office, and sent to command Xi and Li.

sentences.zh: 居二年，徵拜丞相府司馬，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: After two years he was summoned and appointed chancellor's marshal, and advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was recalled to serve as marshal of the chancellor's office and advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 出為北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of North Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed governor of North Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 州帶北山，多有盜賊。

translations.literal: The province bordered the northern mountains and had many bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The province lay along the northern mountains, and banditry was widespread.

sentences.zh: 褒密訪之，並豪右所為也，而陽不之知。

translations.literal: Bao secretly investigated and found they were all the work of powerful local families, yet outwardly he pretended not to know.
translations.idiomatic: Bao investigated in secret and learned that the leading gentry families were behind the raids, yet he feigned ignorance in public.

sentences.zh: 厚加禮遇，謂曰：「刺史起自書生，安知督盜？

translations.literal: He treated them with great courtesy and said, "The governor rose from the scholar class—how could he know how to hunt bandits?
translations.idiomatic: He treated them with elaborate courtesy and said, "I am only a scholar turned governor—what do I know about catching thieves?

sentences.zh: 所賴卿等共分其憂耳。」

translations.literal: I rely on you gentlemen to share this worry with me."
translations.idiomatic: I must rely on you to share this burden with me."

sentences.zh: 乃悉召傑黠少年素為鄉里患者，置為主帥，分其地界，有盜發而不獲者，以故縱論。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned all the clever, sharp youths who had long been a scourge in the districts, made them chief captains, divided their territories, and ruled that if a theft occurred and was not solved, guilt would be assigned by prior release.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the boldest young troublemakers from each district, appointed them chief constables with fixed jurisdictions, and decreed that any unsolved theft in a district would be charged to the constable responsible for it.

sentences.zh: 於是諸被署者莫不惶懼，皆首伏曰：「前盜發者，並某等為之。」

translations.literal: Thereupon all those appointed were fearful; each confessed, saying, "The thefts committed before were all done by us."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, every man he had appointed confessed at once: "We ourselves committed all the earlier robberies."

sentences.zh: 所有徒侶，皆列其姓名，或亡命隱匿者，並悉言其所在。

translations.literal: All their accomplices were listed by name; even those in flight and hiding—they fully disclosed where they were.
translations.idiomatic: They named every accomplice, and even fugitives in hiding—they gave up each man's whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 褒乃取盜名簿藏之，因大榜州門曰：「自知行盜者，可急來首，即除其罪。

translations.literal: Bao then took the register of thieves and hid it, and posted a great notice at the provincial gate: "Those who know themselves to have committed theft may hurry to confess and their crime will be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Bao filed away the roster of names and posted a proclamation at the provincial gate: "Anyone who has committed theft may come forward at once and be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 盡今月不首者，顯戮其身，籍沒妻子，以賞前首者。」

translations.literal: Any who do not confess by the end of this month will be publicly executed, their wives and children registered and confiscated, and the property given as reward to earlier confessors."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who fails to surrender before month's end will be executed in public; his wife and children will be enslaved and their property given to those who have already confessed."

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，諸盜咸悉首盡。

translations.literal: Within ten days all the thieves had fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days every thief in the province had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 褒取名簿勘之，一無差異，並原其罪，許以自新，由是群盜屏息。

translations.literal: Bao took out the name register and checked it—there was not a single discrepancy; he pardoned all their crimes and allowed them to reform, and from this the bandits were stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Bao compared the confessions with his hidden register—not a single name was missing. He pardoned them all and allowed them to start anew, and banditry ceased throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 入為給事黃門侍郎，遷侍中，除都督、西涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He entered office as gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate, was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary, and appointed commander-in-chief and governor of West Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate, promoted to attendant-in-ordinary, and appointed regional commander and governor of West Liang.

sentences.zh: 羌胡之俗，輕貧弱，尚豪富。

translations.literal: The custom among the Qiang and Hu was to despise the poor and weak and honor the rich and powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Qiang and Hu peoples, the poor were despised and the wealthy were revered.

sentences.zh: 豪富之家，侵漁百姓，同于僕錄。

translations.literal: Wealthy powerful houses preyed on the common people as if they were bond servants.
translations.idiomatic: Rich magnates preyed on commoners and treated them like bondsmen.

sentences.zh: 故貧者日削，豪者益富。

translations.literal: Thus the poor daily dwindled and the powerful grew richer.
translations.idiomatic: The poor grew poorer day by day while the powerful grew ever richer.

sentences.zh: 褒乃悉募貧人，以充兵士，優復其家，蠲免徭賦。

translations.literal: Bao then recruited all the poor to fill the ranks as soldiers, gave their households favorable exemption, and remitted corvée and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Bao recruited the poor into military service, granted their households tax relief, and exempted them from corvée and levies.

sentences.zh: 又調富人財物以振給之。

translations.literal: He also levied the wealth of the rich to relieve and supply them.
translations.idiomatic: He also assessed the wealthy and distributed their goods to support the poor.

sentences.zh: 每西城商貨至，又先盡貧者市之。

translations.literal: Whenever western merchants' goods arrived, he again had the poor buy them all first.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever merchant caravans arrived from the west, he gave the poor first chance to buy their goods.

sentences.zh: 於是貧富漸均，戶口殷實。

translations.literal: Thereupon rich and poor gradually equalized, and households grew prosperous and full.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually the gap between rich and poor narrowed, and the population prospered.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元年，為會州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Deposed Emperor, he became governor of Hui Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei he was appointed governor of Hui Province.

sentences.zh: 後以驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公，累遷汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Later, as general of agile cavalry and grand master with staff equal to the Three Excellencies, he advanced in rank to duke and was repeatedly transferred to governor of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made general of agile cavalry with the privilege of an independent staff, advanced to duke, and eventually appointed governor of Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 先是，齊寇數入，人廢耕桑，前後刺史，莫能防扞。

translations.literal: Before this, Qi raiders had repeatedly entered; the people abandoned farming and sericulture; successive governors could not defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi raiders had repeatedly invaded the region, driving the people from their fields; none of Bao's predecessors had been able to stop them.

sentences.zh: 褒至，適會寇來，乃不下屬縣。

translations.literal: When Bao arrived, it happened that raiders came; he did not alert the subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after Bao took office, raiders struck again—but he did not warn the subordinate counties.

sentences.zh: 人既不備，以故多被抄掠。

translations.literal: Since the people were unprepared, for this reason many were plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Caught unprepared, many were robbed.

sentences.zh: 齊人喜於不覺，以為州先未集兵，今還必不能追躡，由是益懈，不為營壘。

translations.literal: The Qi men were pleased at not being detected; they thought the province had not yet gathered troops before, and on returning now surely could not pursue—thereby they grew more slack and did not build camps.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi troops, pleased that no alarm had been raised, assumed the province had no forces ready and that no pursuit would follow. They grew careless and made no fortified camp.

sentences.zh: 褒已先勒精銳，伏北山中，分據險阻，邀其歸路。

translations.literal: Bao had already beforehand mustered elite troops, hidden them in the northern mountains, divided and held the dangerous passes, and blocked their return route.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had already positioned his best troops in ambush in the northern mountains, holding the defiles along the raiders' line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 乘其眾怠，縱伏擊之，盡獲其眾。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of their troops' slackness, he released the ambush and struck them, capturing their entire force.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy relaxed their guard, he sprang the ambush and captured the entire raiding party.

sentences.zh: 故事，獲生口者，並送京師，褒因是奏曰：「所獲賊眾，不足為多，俘而辱之，但益其忿耳。

translations.literal: By precedent, captives taken alive were all sent to the capital; Bao therefore memorialized: "The bandit force captured is not large enough to matter; to hold them captive and humiliate them only increases their rage.
translations.idiomatic: By custom all captives were sent to the capital. Bao memorialized the throne: "These prisoners are too few to matter; holding and humiliating them will only deepen their hatred.

sentences.zh: 請一切放還，以德報怨。」

translations.literal: I ask that they all be released and that enmity be answered with virtue."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that they all be released, so that we may repay enmity with kindness."

sentences.zh: 有詔許焉。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 自此抄兵頗息，遷河州總管，仍轉鳳州刺史。

translations.literal: From this raiding troops largely ceased; he was transferred to commander of He Province, then turned to governor of Feng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Raids largely ceased after this. He was appointed commander of He Province and later transferred to governor of Feng.

sentences.zh: 尋以年老請致事，詔許之。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of age, he requested retirement; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked to retire on grounds of age, and the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 天和五年，拜少保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhe he was appointed junior mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Tianhe era he was appointed junior mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 褒曆事三帝，以忠厚見知。

translations.literal: Bao served through three emperors and was known for loyalty and honesty.
translations.idiomatic: Bao served three emperors and was esteemed for his loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 武帝深相敬重，常以師道處之，每入朝見，必有詔令坐，然始論政事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu deeply respected him, constantly treating him with the ceremony due a teacher; each time he entered court for audience there was always an edict ordering him to be seated before political matters were discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu held him in the highest regard and always treated him as a teacher. Whenever Bao came to court, the emperor would order him seated before any business was discussed.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈涇、岐、燕三州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given the three provincial governorships of Jing, Qi, and Yan; his posthumous name was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously honored with the titles of governor of Jing, Qi, and Yan provinces, and given the posthumous name Zhen (Upright).

sentences.zh: 子繼伯嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jibo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jibo succeeded to his line.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，位終衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: He served Sui and ended his career as vice minister of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he rose to vice minister of the guard.

sentences.zh: 趙肅，字慶壅，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Su, style name Qingyong, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Su, whose style name was Qingyong, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 世仕河西。

translations.literal: His family for generations served in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served in the Hexi region for generations.

sentences.zh: 及沮渠氏滅，曾祖武始歸於魏，賜爵金城侯。

translations.literal: When the Juqu clan was destroyed, his great-grandfather Wu first returned to Wei and was granted the title Marquis of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Juqu regime, his great-grandfather Wu was among the first to submit to Wei and was ennobled as Marquis of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 祖興，中書博士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xing was a doctoral scholar of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xing served as a doctoral scholar in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父申侯，舉秀才，為後軍府主簿。

translations.literal: His father Shenhou was recommended as xiucai and became chief clerk of the Rear Army Office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shenhou passed the provincial examination and served as chief clerk in the Rear Army Office.

sentences.zh: 肅早有操行，知名于時。

translations.literal: Su early had moral conduct and was known in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Su was known from youth for his integrity and won renown in his own day.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，起家殿中侍御史，累遷左將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he first entered office as palace attendant censor, and was repeatedly promoted to left general and grand master of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era he entered service as a palace censor and rose through the ranks to left general and grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 東魏天平初，除新安郡守，秩滿還洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping under Eastern Wei, he was appointed prefect of Xin'an; when his term ended he returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Eastern Wei Tianping era he was appointed prefect of Xin'an; when his term expired he returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，獨孤信東討，肅率宗人為嚮導。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Dugu Xin campaigned eastward; Su led his clansmen as guides.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, when Dugu Xin marched east, Su led his clansmen as guides.

sentences.zh: 授司州別駕，監督糧儲，軍用不匱。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice governor of Si Province, supervised grain stores, and military supplies were not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice governor of Si Province, where he oversaw grain supplies so that the army never wanted for provisions.

sentences.zh: 周文帝聞之，謂人曰：「趙肅可謂洛陽主人也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou heard of this and said to others, "Zhao Su may be called the master of Luoyang."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai heard of this, he remarked, "Zhao Su is truly the master of Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 九年，行華山郡事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he acted as administrator of Huashan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he served as acting administrator of Huashan commandery.

sentences.zh: 十三年，除廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 明年元日，當行朝禮，非有封爵者不得預焉。

translations.literal: The next year on New Year's Day the court ceremony was to be performed; those without enfeoffed rank could not participate.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day the following year, only men holding enfeoffed rank were permitted to attend the court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 肅時未有茅土，左僕射長孫儉啟周文請之，周文乃召肅謂曰：「歲初行禮，豈得使卿不預！

translations.literal: Su at that time had no fief; left vice director Changsun Jian memorialized Zhou Wen to request it; Zhou Wen then summoned Su and said, "At the year's opening ceremony, how can I let you not participate!
translations.idiomatic: Su had not yet received a fief. Left vice director Changsun Jian petitioned Yuwen Tai on his behalf. Yuwen Tai summoned Su and said, "How can I let you miss the New Year ceremony?

sentences.zh: 然何為不早言也？」

translations.literal: Yet why did you not speak of it earlier?"
translations.idiomatic: Why did you not tell me sooner?"

sentences.zh: 於是令肅自選封名。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had Su choose his own enfeoffment name.
translations.idiomatic: He then allowed Su to choose his own fief name.

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「河清乃太平之應，竊所願也。」

translations.literal: Su said, "'The river is clear' is the omen of great peace—this is what I privately wish."
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "'The river runs clear' is the sign of an age of peace—that is the name I would choose."

sentences.zh: 於是封清河縣子。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Qinghe county.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly enfeoffed as Viscount of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 十六年，除廷尉卿，加征東將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed minister of justice and additionally made general who campaigns east.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was appointed minister of justice with the additional title of general who campaigns east.

sentences.zh: 肅久在理官。

translations.literal: Su long served in the office of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Su had long served in the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 執心平允，凡所處斷，咸得其情。

translations.literal: He held the law with fairness; in all cases he decided, he always hit the truth of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He judged with evenhanded fairness, and in every case he decided reached a just outcome.

sentences.zh: 廉慎自居，不營產業，時人以此稱之。

translations.literal: He maintained himself in integrity and caution, did not pursue estates, and people of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He lived modestly and never sought personal gain, for which his contemporaries praised him.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進位車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍，賜姓乙弗氏。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he advanced to general of the chariots and cavalry, equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and irregular attendant-in-ordinary; he was granted the surname Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, appointed irregular attendant-in-ordinary, and granted the surname Yifu.

sentences.zh: 先是，周文命肅撰法律，肅積思累年，遂感心疾。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhou Wen had ordered Su to compile laws; Su piled thought for many years and thereby contracted a heart ailment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yuwen Tai had ordered him to draft a legal code. Su labored over the task for years until he fell ill with a heart condition.

sentences.zh: 去職，卒於家。

translations.literal: He left office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned his post and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子軌。

translations.literal: His son was Gui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gui.

sentences.zh: 軌少好學，有行檢。

translations.literal: Gui in youth loved learning and had moral discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Gui loved learning from youth and was known for his moral discipline.

sentences.zh: 周蔡王引為記室，以清苦聞。

translations.literal: The Zhou Prince of Cai appointed him recorder and he became known for purity and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Cai appointed him recorder on his staff; he became known for his austere integrity.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，為齊州別駕，有能名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he became vice governor of Qi Province and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen founded the Sui dynasty, Gui served as vice governor of Qi Province and earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 其東鄰有桑，葚落其家，軌遣人悉拾還其主，戒其諸子曰：「吾非以此求名，意者非機杼物，不願侵人。

translations.literal: His eastern neighbor had mulberry trees; mulberries fell into his house; Gui sent men to gather them all and return them to the owner, admonishing his sons: "I do not do this to seek a name; my meaning is that what is not from the loom one should not wish to take from others.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberries from his neighbor's tree fell into his courtyard; Gui had every one gathered and returned, then warned his sons: "I am not doing this for reputation. What does not come from one's own loom should never be taken from another.

sentences.zh: 汝等宜以為戒。」

translations.literal: You should take this as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: Take this as your rule."

sentences.zh: 在州考績連最。

translations.literal: In the province his performance evaluations were repeatedly top-ranked.
translations.idiomatic: His performance evaluations in the province were repeatedly the highest in the realm.

sentences.zh: 持節使者郃陽公梁子恭上狀，文帝賜以米帛甚優，令入朝。

translations.literal: The commissioner bearing credentials, Duke of Heyang Liang Zigong, submitted a memorial; Emperor Wen bestowed rice and silk in great generosity and ordered him to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Liang Zigong, Duke of Heyang, reported his excellence to the throne. Emperor Wen rewarded him generously with grain and silk and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 父老將送者，各揮涕曰：「別駕在官，水火不與百姓交，是以不敢以杯酒相送。

translations.literal: The elders who came to see him off each wiped tears and said, "While the vice governor was in office he did not mix fire and water with the common people—therefore we dare not send you off with a cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: The elders who came to see him off wept and said, "While you held office you never accepted so much as a cup of tea from us—we dare not offer you wine now.

sentences.zh: 公清如水，請酌一杯水奉餞。」

translations.literal: Your lordship is clear as water; we beg to offer a cup of water in farewell."
translations.idiomatic: You are pure as water—please accept a cup of water in farewell instead."

sentences.zh: 軌受飲之。

translations.literal: Gui accepted and drank it.
translations.idiomatic: Gui accepted and drank the water.

sentences.zh: 至京，詔與牛弘撰定律令格式。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital, he was ordered together with Niu Hong to compile statutes, ordinances, and formats.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital he was ordered to join Niu Hong in drafting the dynasty's laws and administrative codes.

sentences.zh: 時衛王爽為原州總管，召為司馬。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Wei of Shuang was commander of Yuan Province and summoned him as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei Shuang, regional commander of Yuan Province, then summoned him as his marshal.

sentences.zh: 在道夜行，其左右馬逸入田中，暴人禾。

translations.literal: Traveling on the road at night, the horses of his attendants bolted into the fields and trampled people's grain.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling by night, his attendants' horses broke loose and trampled a farmer's standing grain.

sentences.zh: 軌駐馬待明，訪知禾主，酬直而去。

translations.literal: Gui halted his horse and waited for dawn, inquired and learned the owner of the grain, paid compensation and left.
translations.idiomatic: Gui halted and waited until dawn, found the owner, paid full compensation, and went on.

sentences.zh: 原州人吏聞之，莫不改操。

translations.literal: When the officials and clerks of Yuan Province heard of this, none failed to reform their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When word of this reached the officials of Yuan Province, every one of them resolved to mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 後檢校硤州刺史，甚有恩惠。

translations.literal: Later he was inspector of Xia Province and showed great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as inspector of Xia Province, where he showed great kindness to the people.

sentences.zh: 轉壽州總管長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of the Shouzhou regional headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk at the Shouzhou regional headquarters.

sentences.zh: 芍陂舊有五門堰，蕪穢不通。

translations.literal: At Quepi there was an old dam with five gates, overgrown and impassable.
translations.idiomatic: The old Quepi dam had five sluice gates, but they were choked with weeds and no longer functioned.

sentences.zh: 軌勸課吏人，更開三十六門，灌田五千餘頃，人賴其利。

translations.literal: Gui urged the clerks and people to reopen thirty-six gates, irrigating more than five thousand qing of fields; the people relied on this benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Gui urged officials and commoners to reopen thirty-six gates, irrigating more than five thousand qing of farmland; the people prospered from the project.

sentences.zh: 秩滿歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned home and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned home and died there.

sentences.zh: 子弘安、弘智，並知名。

translations.literal: His sons Hong'an and Hongzhi were both well known.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Hong'an and Hongzhi both won renown.

sentences.zh: 張軌，字元軌，濟北臨邑人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui, style name Yuangui, was a native of Linyi in Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, whose style name was Yuangui, came from Linyi in Jibei.

sentences.zh: 父崇，高平令。

translations.literal: His father Chong was magistrate of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong served as magistrate of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 軌少好學，志識開朗。

translations.literal: Gui in youth loved learning and had open, bright aims and knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Gui loved learning and possessed a keen and far-seeing mind.

sentences.zh: 初在洛陽，家貧，與樂安孫樹仁為莫逆之友，每易衣而出，以此見稱。

translations.literal: Early in Luoyang, his family was poor; he and Sun Shuren of Le'an were sworn friends, each time exchanging clothes before going out—thereby he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: While living in Luoyang in poverty, he and Sun Shuren of Le'an became sworn friends; they would take turns wearing each other's clothes when going out, and people praised them for it.

sentences.zh: 軌常謂所親曰：「秦、雍之間，必有王者。」

translations.literal: Gui often told those close to him, "Between Qin and Yong there is sure to be a king."
translations.idiomatic: Gui often told his intimates, "Between Qin and Yong a true king is bound to arise."

sentences.zh: 爾硃氏敗後，遂杖策入關。

translations.literal: After the Erzhu clan fell, he then took staff in hand and entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Erzhu clan, he took up his staff and made his way into the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 賀拔嶽以軌為記室參軍。

translations.literal: Heba Yue made Gui recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue appointed him recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 典機密。

translations.literal: He managed confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: He handled confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋轉倉曹。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to granary clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to granary clerk.

sentences.zh: 時穀糴踴貴，或有請貸官倉者，軌曰：「以私害公，非吾宿志。

translations.literal: At that time grain prices soared; some asked to borrow from the official granary; Gui said, "To harm the public for private gain is not my longstanding aim.
translations.idiomatic: Grain prices soared; some proposed drawing on the official granaries. Gui said, "To sacrifice the public good for private gain has never been my way.

sentences.zh: 濟人之難，詎得相違？」

translations.literal: To relieve people's hardship—how could I go against that?"
translations.idiomatic: To ease the people's distress—how could I refuse?"

sentences.zh: 乃賣所服衣物，糴粟以振其乏。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sold his own clothing, bought grain, and relieved their want.
translations.idiomatic: He sold his own clothing, bought grain, and distributed it to the needy.

sentences.zh: 及岳被害，周文帝以軌為都督，從征侯莫陳悅。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed, Emperor Wen of Zhou made Gui a commander and followed him in campaigning against Houmochen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue was murdered, Yuwen Tai appointed Gui a commander and took him on the campaign against Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 悅平，使於洛陽，見領軍斛斯椿。

translations.literal: When Yue was pacified, he was sent to Luoyang and met the camp commander Husi Chun.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory he was sent to Luoyang, where he met the camp commander Husi Chun.

sentences.zh: 椿曰：「高歡逆謀，已傳行路，人情西望，以日為年，未知宇文何如賀拔也？」

translations.literal: Chun said, "Gao Huan's rebellious plot is already known on the roads; people's hearts look west, counting the days as years—who knows whether Yuwen is the equal of Heba?"
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "Gao Huan's treason is common talk on every road; all eyes turn westward and each day feels like a year. Who knows whether Yuwen Tai can match Heba Yue?"

sentences.zh: 軌曰：「宇文公文足經國，武足定亂，至於高識遠度，非愚管所測。」

translations.literal: Gui said, "Lord Yuwen's civil arts suffice to govern the state, his martial arts to settle chaos; as for lofty insight and far vision, that is not what my shallow wit can measure."
translations.idiomatic: Gui replied, "Lord Yuwen's civil talents are enough to govern the realm, his martial prowess enough to quell chaos. As for his depth of vision, that is beyond my poor judgment."

sentences.zh: 椿曰：「誠如卿言，真可恃也。」

translations.literal: Chun said, "Truly as you say—he may indeed be relied upon."
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "If that is so, he is truly a man one can trust."

sentences.zh: 周文為行台，授軌郎中。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen became executive agency chief; Gui was appointed gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai became head of the executive agency, Gui was appointed a gentleman on his staff.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，除中書舍人，封壽張縣子，肅著作佐郎，修起居注，遷給事黃門侍郎，兼吏部郎中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Gui was appointed palace secretary, enfeoffed Viscount of Shouzhang, associate draftsman, compiled imperial diaries, was transferred to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate, and concurrently ministerial gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved the capital west, Gui was appointed palace secretary, enfeoffed as Viscount of Shouzhang, appointed associate draftsman and compiler of the imperial diary, then promoted to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate while also serving as ministerial gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出為河北郡守。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Hebei commandery.

sentences.zh: 在郡三年，聲績甚著，臨人政術，有循吏之美。

translations.literal: In the commandery for three years his reputation and achievements were very notable; in governing people his political art had the beauty of a model official.
translations.idiomatic: For three years in the commandery his record was outstanding; in governing the people he displayed the virtues of a model official.

sentences.zh: 大統間言宰人者，多推尚之。

translations.literal: During Datong, those who spoke of chief ministers mostly praised and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Datong era, those who discussed potential chief ministers often singled him out for praise.

sentences.zh: 入為丞相府從事中郎，行武功郡事。

translations.literal: He entered as attendant gentleman of the chancellor's office and acted as administrator of Wugong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as attendant gentleman in the chancellor's office and served as acting administrator of Wugong commandery.

sentences.zh: 章武公導出鎮秦州，以軌為長史。

translations.literal: Duke Zhangwu Dao went out to garrison Qin Province; Gui was made chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Zhangwu Yuwen Dao was sent to garrison Qin Province, Gui served as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元年，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Deposed Emperor, he advanced to general of chariots and cavalry, equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and irregular attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei he was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies and appointed irregular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 二年，賜姓宇文氏，行南秦州事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was granted the surname Yuwen and acted as administrator of South Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was granted the surname Yuwen and served as acting administrator of South Qin.

sentences.zh: 恭帝二年，徵拜度支尚書，復除隴右府長史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gongdi he was summoned as minister of revenue and again appointed chief clerk of the Longyou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong he was summoned as minister of revenue, then reappointed chief clerk of the Longyou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 卒於位，諡曰質。

translations.literal: He died in office; his posthumous name was Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was given the posthumous name Zhi (Plain).

sentences.zh: 軌性清素，臨終之日，家無餘財，唯有書數百卷。

translations.literal: Gui's nature was pure and plain; on the day of his death his house had no surplus wealth—only several hundred volumes of books.
translations.idiomatic: Gui lived plainly; when he died his household held no surplus wealth—only several hundred books.

sentences.zh: 子肅，周明帝初為宣納上士，轉中外府記室參軍、中山公訓侍讀。

translations.literal: His son Su, at the beginning of Emperor Ming of Zhou was attendant for presenting documents, then transferred to recording secretary of the inner and outer offices and reader to Duke Zhongshan Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Su, early in the reign of Emperor Ming of Zhou, served as attendant for presenting documents, then became recording secretary of the inner and outer offices and reader to Duke Zhongshan Yuwen Xun.

sentences.zh: 早有才名，性頗輕猾，時人比之魏諷。

translations.literal: Early he had a reputation for talent; his nature was rather frivolous and cunning; people of the time compared him to Wei Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He won early fame for talent but was rather frivolous and slippery; contemporaries compared him to Wei Feng.

sentences.zh: 卒以罪考竟終。

translations.literal: He ended by dying in prison after examination for crime.
translations.idiomatic: He died in prison after being tried for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 李彥，字彥士，梁郡下邑人也。

translations.literal: Li Yan, style name Yanshi, was a native of Xiayi in Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, whose style name was Yanshi, came from Xiayi in Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖光之，魏淮南郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guangzhi was Wei prefect of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guangzhi served as prefect of Huainan under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父靜，南青州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jing was governor of South Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing was governor of South Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 彥少有節操，好學慕古。

translations.literal: Yan in youth had moral discipline, loved learning and admired antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yan was principled, loved learning, and revered the examples of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，解褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he first took office as court gentleman for attendance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era he entered service as court gentleman for attendance.

sentences.zh: 孝武入關，兼著作佐郎，修起居注。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the passes, he concurrently served as associate draftsman and compiled imperial diaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the Guanzhong region, he also served as associate draftsman compiling the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 大統初，除通直散騎侍郎，累遷左戶郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he was appointed irregular attendant cavalier and was repeatedly promoted to left household gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong he was appointed irregular attendant cavalier and rose to left household gentleman.

sentences.zh: 十二年，省三十六曹為十二部，改授戶部郎中，封平陽縣子。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the thirty-six bureaus were reduced to twelve departments; he was reassigned household gentleman and enfeoffed Viscount of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when the thirty-six bureaus were consolidated into twelve departments, he was reassigned as household gentleman and enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 廢帝初，拜尚書右丞，轉左丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor he was appointed right vice director of the Secretariat, then transferred to left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Fei's reign he was appointed right vice director of the Secretariat, then left vice director.

sentences.zh: 彥在尚書十有五載，屬軍國草創，庶務殷繁，留心省閣，未嘗懈怠。

translations.literal: Yan was in the Secretariat for fifteen years; the state was newly founded and military affairs numerous; he attended to the provincial offices and never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Yan served in the Secretariat for fifteen years. The state was newly founded and affairs were pressing; he attended to his duties in the offices without ever slackening.

sentences.zh: 斷決如流，略無疑滯。

translations.literal: His decisions flowed like water; scarcely a doubt or delay.
translations.idiomatic: His decisions flowed swiftly, with scarcely a hesitation.

sentences.zh: 台閣莫不歎其公勤，服其明察。

translations.literal: None in the offices failed to admire his fairness and diligence and acknowledge his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the bureaucracy admired his diligence and respected his keen judgment.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎，仍左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate while still left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate while retaining his post as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: He was granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 出為鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Fu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Fu Province.

sentences.zh: 六官建，改授軍司馬，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was reassigned army marshal and advanced in rank to baron.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was reassigned as army marshal and advanced to baron.

sentences.zh: 彥性謙恭，有禮節，雖居顯要，於親黨之間恂如也。

translations.literal: Yan's nature was modest and respectful, with ritual propriety; though he held eminent posts, among kin and friends he was still deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was modest and courteous; though he held high office, he remained deferential among kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 輕財重義，好施愛士，時論以此稱之，然素多疾，而勤於蒞職，雖沈頓枕席，猶理務不輟，遂至於卒。

translations.literal: He lightly valued wealth and heavily valued righteousness, loved giving and cherished scholars; opinion for this praised him—yet he had long been ill and was diligent in office; even prostrate on his pillow he did not cease handling affairs, until he died.
translations.idiomatic: He scorned wealth and prized integrity, was generous to scholars, and won praise for it; yet he had long been ill and still drove himself at his duties—even bedridden he never stopped working, until death overtook him.

sentences.zh: 諡曰敬。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Jing (Respectful).

sentences.zh: 彥臨終遺誡其子等曰：「昔人以窾木為櫝，葛累為緘，下不亂泉，上不泄臭，實吾平生之志也。

translations.literal: On his deathbed Yan admonished his sons: "The ancients used hollow wood for a coffin and creeper for bindings—below not disturbing the springs, above not leaking odor—this was truly my lifelong wish.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Yan admonished his sons: "The ancients used hollow logs for coffins and wrapped them in vines—so that below they would not foul the springs and above they would not reek. That has always been my own wish.

sentences.zh: 但事既矯枉，恐為世士所譏。

translations.literal: But the matter is already overcorrected and I fear ridicule from gentlemen of the age.
translations.idiomatic: But times have changed, and I fear gentlemen of the day would mock such austerity.

sentences.zh: 今可斂以時服，葬於磽鹈脊之地，勿用明器、芻塗及儀衛等。

translations.literal: Now you may dress me in timely garments and bury me on barren ridge ground; do not use bright vessels, straw coating, or guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Bury me in my ordinary clothes on some barren hillside; use no grave goods, no plastered mound, and no funeral guard.

sentences.zh: 爾其今哉。」

translations.literal: You must heed this now."
translations.idiomatic: See that you obey this."

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉焉。

translations.literal: The court praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended his wishes.

sentences.zh: 不奪其志。

translations.literal: They did not deny his intent.
translations.idiomatic: They did not override his intent.

sentences.zh: 子升明嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shengming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shengming succeeded to his line.

sentences.zh: 少曆顯職。

translations.literal: In youth he held eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he held high office.

sentences.zh: 大象末，太府中大夫、儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he was grand master of the palace treasury and general with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he was grand master of the palace treasury and a general with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，終於齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He served Sui and ended as governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he rose to governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 子仁政，長安縣長。

translations.literal: His son Renzheng was magistrate of Chang'an county.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renzheng served as magistrate of Chang'an county.

sentences.zh: 義軍至，以罪誅。

translations.literal: When the righteous army arrived, he was executed for crime.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel army reached the capital, he was executed for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 郭彥，太原陽曲人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yan, a native of Yangqu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yan came from Yangqu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 其先從官關右，遂居馮翊。

translations.literal: His ancestors followed official service to the Guan region and thus settled in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had followed official postings into the Guanzhong region and settled in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 父胤，靈武令。

translations.literal: His father Yin was magistrate of Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin served as magistrate of Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 彥少知名。

translations.literal: Yan in youth was known by reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was known by reputation from youth.

sentences.zh: 周文帝臨雍州，辟為西曹書佐。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou held Yong Province, he recruited him as western bureau clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai governed Yong Province, he recruited Yan as western bureau clerk.

sentences.zh: 累遷虞部郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to gentleman of the Parks Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to gentleman of the Parks Bureau.

sentences.zh: 大統十二年，初選當州首望，統領鄉兵，除帥都督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Datong, first selected as leading family head of the province, he commanded district militia and was appointed commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Datong he was chosen as leading head of the provincial gentry, commanded local militia, and was appointed commander.

sentences.zh: 以居郎官著稱，封龍門縣子，進大都督。

translations.literal: For his excellence as a court gentleman he was enfeoffed Viscount of Longmen and advanced to grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: For distinguished service as a court gentleman he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Longmen and promoted to grand commander.

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年，除兵部尚書，仍以本兵從柱國于謹南伐江陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gongdi he was appointed minister of war and with his original troops followed the pillar of state Yu Jin in the southern campaign against Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong he was appointed minister of war and, retaining his original command, followed the pillar of state Yu Jin on the southern campaign against Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: He advanced to general of agile cavalry, grand master with staff equal to the Three Excellencies, and advanced in rank to baron.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of agile cavalry with an independent staff equal to the Three Excellencies and advanced to baron.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜戶部中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed grand master of the Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed grand master of the Household Bureau.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，出為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, he went out as governor of Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Yan was appointed governor of Li Province.

sentences.zh: 蠻左生梗，不營農業。

translations.literal: The southern barbarians were stubborn and did not practice agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: The indigenous peoples of the region were unruly and did not farm.

sentences.zh: 彥勸以耕稼，人皆務本，亡命之徒，咸從賦役。

translations.literal: Yan urged them to plow and plant; all turned to the fundamental occupation; fugitives all submitted to tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Yan urged them to farm; the people took to agriculture, and fugitives returned to pay taxes and perform corvée.

sentences.zh: 先是，以澧州糧儲乏少，每令荊州遞送。

translations.literal: Before this, because Li Province's grain stores were scant, grain was always relayed from Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Li Province's granaries had been empty, and grain had to be shipped in from Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 自彥蒞職，倉庾充實，無復轉輸之勞。

translations.literal: From the time Yan took office, the granaries were full and there was no more relay transport.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan took office the granaries were full and the costly relay shipments ceased.

sentences.zh: 齊南安城主馮顯密遣使歸降，其眾未之知也。

translations.literal: Feng Xian, lord of Nan'an in Qi, secretly sent envoys to surrender; his troops did not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xian, the Qi lord of Nan'an, secretly sent envoys to surrender, but his troops did not yet know.

sentences.zh: 柱國宇文貴令彥率兵應接。

translations.literal: The pillar Yuwen Gui ordered Yan to lead troops to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: The pillar Yuwen Gui ordered Yan to lead troops to meet the defector.

sentences.zh: 時齊人先令顯率所部送糧南下，彥懼其眾不從命，乃于路邀之，顯因得自拔。

translations.literal: The Qi had first ordered Xian to lead his command south delivering grain; Yan feared the troops would not obey and therefore intercepted them on the road; Xian thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi had ordered Xian to march south with grain; Yan, fearing the troops would not follow orders, intercepted them on the road, allowing Xian to escape.

sentences.zh: 其眾果拒戰，彥縱兵奮擊，並虜獲之。

translations.literal: The troops indeed refused battle; Yan unleashed his army and struck fiercely, capturing them all.
translations.idiomatic: The troops indeed resisted; Yan attacked fiercely and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 以南安無備，即引軍掩襲，遂有其城。

translations.literal: Because Nan'an was unprepared, he led his army in a surprise raid and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an was undefended; he led a surprise attack and seized the city.

sentences.zh: 晉公護嘉之，進爵懷德縣公。

translations.literal: Duke Jin of Jin praised him and advanced his rank to Duke of Huaide county.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jin Yuwen Hu commended him and advanced his rank to Duke of Huaide.

sentences.zh: 入為工部中大夫。

translations.literal: He entered office as grand master of the Works Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as grand master of the Works Bureau.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，晉公護東討，彥從尉遲迥攻洛陽，迥復令彥與權景宣出汝南。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, Duke Jin campaigned east; Yan followed Yuchi Jiong in attacking Luoyang; Jiong again ordered Yan with Quan Jingxuan to go out toward Runan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding, Duke Jin marched east; Yan followed Yuchi Jiong in the attack on Luoyang, and Jiong then ordered Yan and Quan Jingxuan to advance toward Runan.

sentences.zh: 及軍次豫州，使彥鎮之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Yu Province, he had Yan garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Yu Province, Jiong left Yan to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 天和中，為隴右總管府長史。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era he was chief clerk of the Longyou regional headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe era he served as chief clerk of the Longyou regional headquarters.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈小司空、宜鄜丹三州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given minor minister of works and the three provincial governorships of Yi, Fu, and Dan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as minor minister of works and governor of Yi, Fu, and Dan provinces.

sentences.zh: 梁昕，字元明，安定烏氏人也。

translations.literal: Liang Xin, style name Yuanming, was a native of Wushi in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xin, whose style name was Yuanming, came from Wushi in Anding.

sentences.zh: 世為關中著姓。

translations.literal: For generations his family was a prominent surname of Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been a leading clan of the Guanzhong region for generations.

sentences.zh: 其先因官，徙居京兆之盩厔。

translations.literal: His ancestors, following official posts, moved to reside in Zhouzhi in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had moved to Zhouzhi in Jingzhao following official postings.

sentences.zh: 祖重耳，漳縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhong'er was magistrate of Zhang County.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhong'er served as magistrate of Zhang County.

sentences.zh: 父勸儒，中散大夫，贈涇州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Quanru was Palace Attendant; posthumously made Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quanru held the post of Palace Attendant and was posthumously appointed Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 昕少溫恭，見稱州裏。

translations.literal: Xin in youth was gentle and deferential, praised within the province.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Liang Xin was gentle and courteous, and was well regarded throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 從爾硃天光征討，拜右將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Following Erzhu Tianguang on punitive campaigns, he was appointed General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Reception.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Tianguang on campaign and was appointed General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Reception.

sentences.zh: 周文帝迎魏孝武，軍次雍州，昕以三輔望族上謁。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou welcomed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei; the army halted at Yong Province; Xin, as scion of an eminent family of the Three Metropolises, went up to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou went to welcome Emperor Xiaowu of Wei and halted his army at Yong Province, Liang Xin—of a leading family of the Three Metropolises—presented himself at court.

sentences.zh: 周文見昕容貌瑰偉，深賞異之，即授右府長流參軍。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen saw Xin's appearance grand and imposing, deeply admired and marked him out, and immediately appointed him chief flowing staff officer of the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen was struck by Liang Xin's imposing presence, took a strong liking to him at once, and appointed him chief flowing staff officer of the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 累遷丞相府主簿。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became chief clerk of the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to become chief clerk of the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 大統十二年，除河南郡守，遷東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Datong he was appointed Administrator of Henan Commandery and transferred to Governor of East Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Datong he was made Administrator of Henan Commandery and then transferred to Governor of East Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 昕撫以仁惠，蠻夷悅之。

translations.literal: Xin governed them with benevolence and kindness; the barbarians were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with benevolence and kindness, winning the goodwill of the non-Han peoples.

sentences.zh: 封安定縣子。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anding County.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anding County.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master with an independent office and ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou came to the throne, Liang Xin was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry with an independent office and ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，進爵胡城縣伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, he was advanced in rank to Baron of Hucheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Ming, he was raised to Baron of Hucheng County.

sentences.zh: 天和初，拜工部中大夫，出為陝州總管府長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, he was appointed Grand Master of the Ministry of Works; sent out as chief clerk of the Shanzhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianhe era he was appointed Grand Master of the Ministry of Works, then went out to serve as chief clerk of the Shanzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 昕性溫裕，有幹能，曆官內外，咸著聲稱。

translations.literal: Xin's nature was mild and generous; he had capacity and ability; through offices inner and outer, all achieved notable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and generous by nature, he possessed real administrative talent; in office after office, at court and in the provinces alike, he earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Great General; posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Great General and given the posthumous name Zhen ("Upright").

sentences.zh: 昕弟榮，位計部下大夫、開府儀同三司、朝那縣伯。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brother Rong held the post of Grand Master of the Bureau of Accounts, Grand Master with an independent office and ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and Baron of Chaona County.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xin's younger brother Rong rose to Grand Master of the Bureau of Accounts, with an independent office and rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Chaona County.

sentences.zh: 贈涇、寧、幽三州刺史，諡曰靜。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Governor of the three provinces Jing, Ning, and You; posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Governor of Jing, Ning, and You provinces and given the posthumous name Jing ("Calm").

sentences.zh: 子蠙，仕隋，為給事郎。

translations.literal: His son Bin served Sui as Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin served under the Sui as an Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，終於鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, he ended as Governor of Zheng Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he died while serving as Governor of Zheng Province.

sentences.zh: 皇甫璠，字景瑜，安定三水人也。

translations.literal: Huang Fufan, style name Jingyu, was a native of Sanshui in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Fufan, whose style name was Jingyu, came from Sanshui in Anding.

sentences.zh: 世為西州著姓，後徙居京兆。

translations.literal: For generations his family was a prominent surname of West Province; later they moved to reside in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been a leading clan of West Province for generations before later moving to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父和，本州中從事。

translations.literal: His father He was middle attendant of the province.
translations.idiomatic: His father He served as middle attendant of the province.

sentences.zh: 大統末，追贈散騎常侍、儀同三司、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong, posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Casual Riding, Grand Master with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Datong era he was posthumously appointed Regular Attendant of the Casual Riding, with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 璠少忠謹，有幹略，永安中，辟州都督。

translations.literal: Fan in youth was loyal and careful, with capacity and strategic insight; in Yongan the provincial military commissioner recruited him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Huang Fufan was loyal and conscientious and showed both administrative talent and strategic insight; in the Yongan era the provincial military commissioner recruited him into service.

sentences.zh: 周文帝為牧，補主簿，以勤事被知。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was regional governor, he was supplemented as chief clerk; for diligent service he was noticed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou served as regional governor, Huang Fufan was appointed chief clerk and came to notice for his diligent service.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，引為丞相府行參軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong, he was brought in as acting staff officer of the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong he was brought into the chancellor's office as an acting staff officer.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，為守廟下大夫、長樂縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was made Grand Master Keeper of the Temples and Viscount of Changle County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou came to the throne, he was appointed Grand Master Keeper of the Temples and enfeoffed as Viscount of Changle County.

sentences.zh: 保定中，為鴻州刺史，入為小納言。

translations.literal: During Baoding, he was Governor of Hong Province; he entered court as Junior Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoding era he served as Governor of Hong Province, then returned to court as Junior Remonstrance Officer.

sentences.zh: 累遷蕃部中大夫，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Grand Master of the Barbarian Affairs Bureau; he was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master with an independent office and ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Grand Master of the Barbarian Affairs Bureau and was then promoted to General of Agile Cavalry with an independent office and ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 璠性平和，小心奉法，安貞守志，恆以清白自處，當時稱為善人。

translations.literal: Fan's nature was even and peaceful; careful in following the law; steadfast in integrity; always conducted himself with spotless purity; contemporaries called him a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Even-tempered and law-abiding, he held fast to his principles and always kept himself above reproach; his contemporaries called him a man of true goodness.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，為隨州刺史，政存簡惠，百姓安之，卒官，贈交、渭二州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he was Governor of Sui Province; his governance maintained simplicity and kindness; the people were at peace; he died in office; posthumously made Governor of the two provinces Jiao and Wei; posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande he became Governor of Sui Province, governing with simplicity and kindness so that the people lived in peace; he died in office and was posthumously appointed Governor of Jiao and Wei provinces, with the posthumous name Gong ("Respectful").

sentences.zh: 子諒，少知名。

translations.literal: His son Liang was known by reputation from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liang was already well known while still young.

sentences.zh: 大象中，位吏部下大夫。

translations.literal: During Daxiang, he held the post of Grand Master of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daxiang era he served as Grand Master of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 諒弟誕。

translations.literal: Liang's younger brother Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's younger brother was Dan.

sentences.zh: 誕字玄慮，少剛毅，有器局，開皇中，累遷治書侍御史，朝臣入不肅憚焉。

translations.literal: Dan, style name Xuanchen, in youth was resolute and firm, with breadth of vision; in Kaihuang, through successive promotions he became Imperial Censor; court ministers on entering did not treat him with casual disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, whose style name was Xuanchen, was resolute and far-sighted from youth; during the Kaihuang era he rose through successive posts to Imperial Censor, and ministers entering his presence did not dare treat him lightly.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Later he became Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時漢王諒為并州總管，朝廷盛選僚佐，拜誕并州總管司馬，總府政事，一以諮之，諒甚敬焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Han, Liang, was military commissioner of Bingzhou; the court carefully selected staff; Dan was appointed chief administrator of the Bingzhou headquarters; all headquarters affairs were entirely referred to him; Liang greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Liang of Han served as military commissioner of Bingzhou, and the court chose his staff with great care; Dan was appointed chief administrator of the headquarters, and Prince Liang entrusted all administrative affairs to him and held him in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝即位，諒用諮議王頍謀，發兵作亂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Liang adopted the counsel of adviser Wang Pi and raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Prince Liang followed the advice of his counselor Wang Pi and raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 誕數諫止，諒不納。

translations.literal: Dan repeatedly remonstrated to stop him; Liang did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Dan remonstrated with him again and again, but Prince Liang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 誕因流涕，以死固請。

translations.literal: Dan thereupon wept and, with his life, firmly pleaded.
translations.idiomatic: Dan wept and pleaded with him, swearing he would rather die than assent.

sentences.zh: 諒怒囚之。

translations.literal: Liang in anger imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang flew into a rage and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 及楊素將至，諒屯清源以拒之。

translations.literal: When Yang Su was about to arrive, Liang stationed troops at Qingyuan to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Su was approaching, Prince Liang massed his troops at Qingyuan to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 諒主簿豆盧毓出誕於獄，協謀閉城拒諒。

translations.literal: Liang's chief clerk Dou Lu Yu released Dan from prison; together they plotted to shut the city gates and resist Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang's chief clerk Dou Lu Yu released Dan from prison, and together they plotted to shut the city gates and resist the prince.

sentences.zh: 諒襲擊破之，並抗節遇害。

translations.literal: Liang launched a raid and broke them; both died upholding their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang attacked and defeated them; both men were killed while steadfastly refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 帝以亡身殉國，嘉悼者久之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he gave his life for the state, praised and mourned him for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, honoring Dan for having sacrificed his life for the state, praised and mourned him at length.

sentences.zh: 詔贈柱國，封弘義公，諡曰明。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Pillar of State, enfeoffed him as Duke of Hongyi, and gave the posthumous title Ming.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously appointed him Pillar of State, enfeoffed him as Duke of Hongyi, and gave him the posthumous name Ming ("Clear-sighted").

sentences.zh: 子無逸嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wuyi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuyi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 尋為淯陽太守，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Administrator of Yuyang; he had a very strong reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Administrator of Yuyang and earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 大業初，令行，舊爵例除。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, the order took effect; old ranks by precedent were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye era the new order took effect, and inherited ranks were abolished by precedent.

sentences.zh: 以無逸誠義之後，賜爵平輿侯。

translations.literal: Because Wuyi was heir to loyalty and righteousness, he was granted the rank Marquis of Pingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wuyi was the heir of a man of loyalty and righteousness, he was granted the rank of Marquis of Pingyu.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部侍郎，守右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments and held the post of General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments and served concurrently as General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 初，漢王諒之反，州縣莫不回應。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Prince of Han, Liang, rebelled, prefectures and counties none failed to respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liang of Han first rebelled, nearly every prefecture and county rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 有嵐州司馬陶世模、繁畤令敬釗，並抗節不從。

translations.literal: There were Lan Prefecture chief administrator Tao Shimou and Fanzhi magistrate Jing Zhao; both upheld their integrity and did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: But Lan Prefecture chief administrator Tao Shimou and Fanzhi magistrate Jing Zhao both held firm and refused to join him.

sentences.zh: 世模，京兆人。

translations.literal: Shimou was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shimou was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 性明敏，有器幹。

translations.literal: His nature was bright and keen; he had administrative capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and quick-witted, he possessed real administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，為嵐州司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou, he was chief administrator of Lan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Renshou era he served as chief administrator of Lan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 諒反，刺史喬鐘葵將赴之，世模以義拒之。

translations.literal: When Liang rebelled, Inspector Qiao Zhongkui was about to go join him; Shimou on grounds of righteousness refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liang rebelled, Inspector Qiao Zhongkui prepared to go over to him, but Shimou refused on grounds of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 臨之以兵，辭氣不撓，鐘葵義而釋之。

translations.literal: Confronted with troops, his words and bearing did not bend; Zhongkui, moved by righteousness, released him.
translations.idiomatic: Though threatened with force, he did not waver in word or bearing; Zhongkui, respecting his integrity, set him free.

sentences.zh: 軍吏請斬之，於是被囚。

translations.literal: Military clerks requested his execution; thereupon he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates demanded his execution, and he was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 及諒平，拜開府，授大興令。

translations.literal: When Liang was pacified, he was appointed with an independent office and given the post of Magistrate of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was put down, he was granted an independent office and appointed Magistrate of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 從衛玄擊楊玄感，以功進位銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Following Wei Xuan in attacking Yang Xuangan, for merit he was advanced to Silver Radiance Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wei Xuan in the campaign against Yang Xuangan and, for his service, was promoted to Silver Radiance Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 釗字積善，河東蒲阪人。

translations.literal: Zhao, style name Jishan, was a native of Puban in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, whose style name was Jishan, came from Puban in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父元約，周布憲中大夫。

translations.literal: His father Yuanyue was Grand Master of the Bureau of Proclamations and Edicts under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanyue served under the Zhou as Grand Master of the Bureau of Proclamations and Edicts.

sentences.zh: 釗，仁壽中為繁畤令，甚有能名。

translations.literal: Zhao, during Renshou served as Magistrate of Fanzhi and had a very strong reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era Zhao served as Magistrate of Fanzhi and earned a strong reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，師陷其城，賊帥墨弼執送偽將喬鐘葵，署為代州總管司馬。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Han, Liang, rebelled, troops captured his city; the bandit chief Mo Bi seized and sent him to the rebel general Qiao Zhongkui, who appointed him chief administrator of the Daizhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liang of Han rebelled, rebel troops took his city; the bandit leader Mo Bi seized him and handed him over to the rebel general Qiao Zhongkui, who appointed him chief administrator of the Daizhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 釗正色拒之，誓之以死。

translations.literal: Zhao with stern countenance refused and swore by his death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao refused with a stern face, swearing he would rather die.

sentences.zh: 會鐘葵敗，釗遂免。

translations.literal: When Zhongkui was defeated, Zhao was thereby released.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongkui was defeated, Zhao was released.

sentences.zh: 卒於朝邑令。

translations.literal: He died as Magistrate of Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Magistrate of Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 辛慶之，字余慶，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Xin Qingzhi, style name Yuqing, was a native of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qingzhi, whose style name was Yuqing, came from Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 世為隴右著姓。

translations.literal: For generations his family was a prominent clan of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been a leading clan of the Longyou region for generations.

sentences.zh: 父顯宗，馮翊郡守，贈雍州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xianzong was Administrator of Feny Commandery; posthumously made Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianzong served as Administrator of Feny Commandery and was posthumously appointed Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 慶之少以文學徵詣洛陽，對策第一，除秘書郎。

translations.literal: Qingzhi in youth was summoned to Luoyang for literary learning; ranked first in the palace examination; appointed Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xin Qingzhi was summoned to Luoyang on account of his literary learning, placed first in the palace examination, and appointed Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 屬爾硃氏作亂，魏孝莊帝令司空楊津為北道行台，節度山東諸軍以討之。

translations.literal: When the Erzhu clan rebelled, Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei ordered Minister of Works Yang Jin as northern route mobile headquarters to coordinate the armies of Shandong to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Erzhu clan rose in rebellion, Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei appointed Minister of Works Yang Jin northern route mobile headquarters commissioner to command the armies of Shandong against them.

sentences.zh: 津啟慶之為行台左丞，與參謀議。

translations.literal: Jin recommended Qingzhi as left assistant of the mobile headquarters and had him join in planning counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jin recommended Xin Qingzhi as left assistant of the mobile headquarters and brought him into strategic deliberations.

sentences.zh: 至鄴，聞孝莊帝崩，遂出兗、冀間，謀結義徒，以赴國難。

translations.literal: Reaching Ye, he heard Emperor Xiaozhuang had died; then he went out between Yan and Ji provinces, plotting to rally volunteers to meet the national crisis.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Ye and learned that Emperor Xiaozhuang had died, he went out into the region between Yan and Ji provinces to rally loyal volunteers against the national crisis.

sentences.zh: 尋而節閔帝立，乃還洛陽。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Jiemin was enthroned; then he returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin was soon enthroned, he returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及賀拔嶽為行台，復啟慶之為行台吏部郎。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue became mobile headquarters commissioner, he again recommended Qingzhi as Personnel Director of the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue became mobile headquarters commissioner, he again recommended Xin Qingzhi as Personnel Director of the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 大統初，從周文帝東討，為行台左丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, following Emperor Wen of Zhou on an eastern campaign, he served as left assistant of the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Datong era he followed Emperor Wen of Zhou on campaign in the east and served as left assistant of the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 六年，行河東郡事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he acted as administrator of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as acting administrator of Hedong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 九年，入為丞相府右長史，兼給事黃門侍郎，除度支尚書，復行河東郡事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he entered court as right chief clerk of the chancellor's office, concurrently Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; appointed Minister of Revenue; again acted as administrator of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he entered the chancellor's office as right chief clerk, concurrently served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, was appointed Minister of Revenue, and again acted as administrator of Hedong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 遷南荊州刺史，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of South Jing Province and given added ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of South Jing Province with added ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 慶之位遇雖隆，而率性儉素，車馬衣服亦不尚華侈。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's position and treatment though lofty, yet by nature he was frugal and plain; carriages, horses, and clothes also did not favor luxury.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xin Qingzhi's rank and favor were great, he remained by nature frugal and plain, never indulging in lavish carriages, horses, or dress.

sentences.zh: 志量淹和，有儒者風度，特為當時所重。

translations.literal: His ambition and capacity were broad and mild; he had the bearing of a Confucian scholar; he was especially valued by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Broad-minded and even-tempered, he carried the bearing of a Confucian gentleman and was especially esteemed in his own day.

sentences.zh: 又以其經明行修。
