translations.literal: Also because of his mastery of the classics and cultivated conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was also accomplished in the classics and upright in conduct,

sentences.zh: 令與盧誕等教授諸王。

translations.literal: He was ordered, together with Lu Dan and others, to instruct the princes.
translations.idiomatic: he was ordered to join Lu Dan and others in instructing the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 慶帝二年，拜秘書監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingdi, he was appointed Director of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Fei Emperor's reign, he was appointed Director of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子加陵，主寢上士。

translations.literal: His son Jialing was Senior Gentleman of the Principal Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jialing served as Senior Gentleman of the Principal Palace.

sentences.zh: 慶之族子昂。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's clansman Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Among Xin Qingzhi's clansmen was Ang.

sentences.zh: 昂字進君。

translations.literal: Ang, style name Jinjun.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's style name was Jinjun.

sentences.zh: 數歲便有成人志行。

translations.literal: At several years of age he already had the aspirations and conduct of a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: Even at a few years of age he already showed the resolve and conduct of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 有善相人者，謂其父仲略曰：「公家雖世載冠冕，然名德富貴，莫有及此兒者。」

translations.literal: A man skilled at physiognomy said to his father Zhonglue: "Your house, though for generations it has borne official hats and rank, yet in fame, virtue, wealth, and honor none has reached this child".
translations.idiomatic: A man skilled in reading faces said to Ang's father Zhonglue: "Your family has borne official rank for generations, yet in fame, virtue, wealth, and honor none of your forebears has matched this boy".

sentences.zh: 仲略亦重昂志氣。

translations.literal: Zhonglue also valued Ang's spirited resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglue himself also set great store by Ang's spirited resolve.

sentences.zh: 深以為然。

translations.literal: He deeply regarded it as so.
translations.idiomatic: He fully agreed.

sentences.zh: 年十八，侯景辟為行台郎中。

translations.literal: At age eighteen, Hou Jing recruited him as mobile headquarters attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was recruited by Hou Jing as an attendant of the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 景後來附，昂遂入朝，除丞相府行參軍。

translations.literal: When Jing later came to submit, Ang then entered court; appointed acting staff officer of the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing later submitted to the court, Ang entered imperial service and was appointed acting staff officer of the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 後追論歸朝勳，封襄城縣男。

translations.literal: Later, in reviewing merit for returning to court, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when merit for returning to the court was reviewed, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangcheng County.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥伐蜀，昂占募從軍。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong campaigned against Shu, Ang recruited volunteers and followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong marched against Shu, Ang recruited volunteers and joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，迥表昂為龍州長史，領龍安郡事。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, Jiong memorialized Ang as chief administrator of Long Province, overseeing Long'an Commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified, Yuchi Jiong memorialized that Ang be appointed chief administrator of Long Province with charge of Long'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 州帶山谷，舊俗生梗。

translations.literal: The province bordered mountains and valleys; the old customs were stubborn and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: The province lay among mountains and valleys, and local custom was harsh and intractable.

sentences.zh: 昂威惠洽著，吏人畏而愛之。

translations.literal: Ang's authority and kindness were thoroughly manifest; officials and people both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's blend of stern authority and gracious kindness was widely felt; officials and commoners alike stood in awe of him yet held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 成都一方之會，風俗舛雜，迥以昂達于從政，復表昂行成都令。

translations.literal: Chengdu was a meeting place for one region; customs were confused and mixed. Jiong, because Ang was skilled in government, again memorialized that Ang act as magistrate of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu was the hub of the region, and its customs were tangled and disorderly. Knowing Ang's talent for administration, Yuchi Jiong again memorialized the court to appoint him acting magistrate of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 昂到縣。

translations.literal: Ang arrived at the county.
translations.idiomatic: When Ang reached the county seat.

sentences.zh: 便與諸生與祭文翁學堂，因共歡宴，謂諸生曰：「子孝臣忠，師嚴友信，立身之要，如斯而已。

translations.literal: He immediately joined the students in offering sacrifice at the Wen Weng Academy, then shared a joyful feast with them, saying to the students: "Filial as sons, loyal as ministers, strict toward teachers, trustworthy toward friends—the essentials of establishing oneself are no more than this.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he arrived, he joined the students in worship at the Wen Weng Academy, then shared a celebratory feast with them and said: "Be filial sons and loyal ministers; be reverent toward teachers and true toward friends—that is the whole foundation of a worthy life.

sentences.zh: 若不事斯語，何以成名？

translations.literal: If you do not attend to these words, how can you achieve a renowned name?
translations.idiomatic: If you do not live by these precepts, how will you ever win a name worth keeping?

sentences.zh: 各宜自勉，克成令譽。」

translations.literal: Each of you should encourage yourselves to fulfill a fine reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Every one of you should strive on your own account to earn an honorable name".

sentences.zh: 昂言切理至，諸生等並深感悟，歸而告其父老曰：「辛君教誡如此，不可違之。」

translations.literal: Ang's words were incisive and perfectly reasoned; the students were all deeply moved. Returning home they told their elders: "Master Xin's admonitions are such as these—we cannot disobey them."
translations.idiomatic: Ang spoke with such force and clarity that every student was deeply stirred. When they went home, they told their elders: "The admonitions of Master Xin are not to be disobeyed".

sentences.zh: 於是井邑肅然，咸從其化。

translations.literal: Thereupon villages and towns became orderly; all followed his transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the villages and market towns fell quiet and orderly, and all submitted to his reforming influence.

sentences.zh: 遷梓潼郡守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be governor of Zitong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Zitong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 六官建，入為司隸上士，襲爵繁昌縣公。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he entered service as senior officer of the Sili, and inherited the title Duke of Fanchang County.
translations.idiomatic: After the Six Offices system was instituted, he was appointed senior officer in the Sili inspectorate and succeeded to the title Duke of Fanchang County.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，為小吏部。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he served as junior director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding (562), he was made junior director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時益州殷阜，軍國所資，經途艱險，每苦劫盜。

translations.literal: At that time Yizhou was prosperous and fertile, providing resources for army and state; the routes were perilous, and banditry was a constant affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou was then rich and fertile—the source of supplies for army and state—but the transport routes were treacherous and brigands were a constant scourge.

sentences.zh: 詔昂使于益、梁，軍人之務皆委決焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ang to go as envoy to Yi and Liang; all military affairs were entrusted to his judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ang to Yi and Liang provinces; all military matters there were placed entirely in his hands.

sentences.zh: 昂撫導荒梗，頗得寧靜。

translations.literal: Ang pacified and guided the rugged frontier regions, achieving considerable tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: Ang soothed and guided the wild borderlands until a measure of peace was restored.

sentences.zh: 天和初，陸騰討信州蠻，詔昂便於通、渠等州運糧饋之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, Lu Teng campaigned against the Man of Xinxhou; an edict ordered Ang to transport grain from Tong, Qu, and other provinces to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianhe era (566), when Lu Teng marched against the Xinxhou tribes, the court ordered Ang to haul grain from Tong, Qu, and neighboring provinces to feed the campaign.

sentences.zh: 時臨、信、楚、合等諸州人庶多從逆，昂諭以禍福，赴者如歸。

translations.literal: At that time the common people of Lin, Xin, Chu, He, and other provinces largely followed the rebels. Ang instructed them regarding fortune and disaster, and those who came to him did so as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Many people in Lin, Xin, Chu, He, and other provinces had joined the rebels, but when Ang reasoned with them about reward and ruin, they flocked to him as gladly as men returning home.

sentences.zh: 乃令老弱負糧，壯夫拒戰，莫有怨者。

translations.literal: He then ordered the old and weak to carry grain and the strong men to resist in battle; none complained.
translations.idiomatic: He put the old and weak to carrying grain and the able-bodied men to fighting—and not one man murmured against it.

sentences.zh: 使還，屬巴州萬榮郡人反叛，圍郡城，昂於是遂募通、開二州，得三千人，倍道兼行，出其不意。

translations.literal: When his mission ended and he was returning, people of Wanrong Commandery in Bazhou rebelled and besieged the commandery city. Ang thereupon recruited from Tong and Kai provinces, obtaining three thousand men, marched at double speed day and night, and struck unexpectedly.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back, the people of Wanrong Commandery in Bazhou rose in revolt and besieged the commandery seat. Ang promptly raised three thousand men from Tong and Kai, forced a double-time march, and fell upon the rebels before they expected it.

sentences.zh: 又令其眾皆作中國歌，直趣賊壘。

translations.literal: He also ordered his troops all to sing songs of China and go straight toward the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: He also had his men sing Chinese songs as they marched straight for the rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 謂有大軍赴救，望風瓦解。

translations.literal: Thinking a great army was coming to the rescue, the rebels dispersed at the mere sight of them.
translations.idiomatic: Believing a large relief force was at hand, the rebels broke apart at the first sign of them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其權以濟事，詔梁州總管、杞國公亮即於軍中賞昂奴婢二十口，繒彩四百匹。

translations.literal: The court praised his expedient measures for achieving the task; an edict ordered Liang Province regional commander, Duke of Qi State Liang, to reward Ang in camp with twenty slaves and four hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The court applauded his resourcefulness in bringing the affair to success and ordered Liangzhou's regional commander, Duke Liang of Qi, to reward Ang on the spot with twenty household slaves and four hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又以昂威信布于宕梁，遂表為渠州刺史。

translations.literal: Because Ang's prestige and trust had spread through Dangliang, he was memorialized for appointment as governor of Qu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Since Ang's authority and credibility now reached throughout Dangliang, the court memorialized him for appointment as governor of Qu Province.

sentences.zh: 轉通州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 推誠布信，甚得夷獠歡心。

translations.literal: He extended sincerity and spread good faith, greatly winning the hearts of the Yi and Liao peoples.
translations.idiomatic: By treating them with open sincerity and steadfast trust, he won the deep loyalty of the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 秩滿還京，首領皆隨昂詣闕朝覲。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, tribal chiefs all followed Ang to the palace to pay court audience.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, tribal chiefs accompanied him to court for an imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 以昂化洽夷落，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Because Ang's transforming influence had reached the barbarian settlements, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Commissioner with the Same Privileges as a Three-in-One Grand Officer.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his civilizing work among the frontier tribes, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry with the privilege of an independent command equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護執政，昂稍被護親待，武帝頗銜之。

translations.literal: At that time Duke of Jin Hu held power; Ang came gradually to enjoy Hu's intimate favor, and Emperor Wu harbored considerable resentment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held the reins of government, and Ang gradually won Hu's personal favor—a fact that Emperor Wu took rather badly.

sentences.zh: 及誅護，加之捶楚，因此遂卒。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, Ang was subjected to beating and torture and thereby died.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was put to death, Ang was beaten and flogged as well and died from it.

sentences.zh: 昂族人仲景，好學，有雅量。

translations.literal: Ang's clansman Zhongjing loved learning and possessed refined magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's kinsman Zhongjing was fond of study and possessed a generous, refined temperament.

sentences.zh: 其高祖欽，後趙吏部尚書、雍州刺史，子孫因家焉。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Qin was Minister of Personnel and governor of Yong Province under Later Zhao; the descendants settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Qin had been Minister of Personnel and governor of Yong Province under Later Zhao, and the family had settled there.

sentences.zh: 父歡，魏隴州刺史、硃陽公。

translations.literal: His father Huan was governor of Long Province in Wei and Duke of Zhuyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huan served Wei as governor of Long Province and held the title Duke of Zhuyang.

sentences.zh: 仲景年十八，舉文學，對策高第。

translations.literal: At eighteen, Zhongjing was recommended for literary learning and ranked at the top in the policy examination.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen Zhongjing was nominated for the literary examination and placed at the head of the policy debate.

sentences.zh: 拜司空府主簿。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief clerk in the office of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk in the Minister of Works' office.

sentences.zh: 建德中，位內史下大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: During Jiande, he held the posts of junior grand master of the Inner Scribe and Commissioner with Same Privileges as the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiande era he rose to junior grand master of the Inner Scribe with the same privileges as a Three Departments commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 子衡。

translations.literal: His son was Heng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Heng.

sentences.zh: 王子直，字孝正，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zizhi, courtesy name Xiaozheng, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zizhi, courtesy name Xiaozheng, came from Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 世為郡右族。

translations.literal: For generations his family was a leading clan of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been one of the commandery's foremost houses.

sentences.zh: 父琳，州主簿、東雍州長史。

translations.literal: His father Lin was provincial chief clerk and chief administrator of eastern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lin had been provincial chief clerk and chief administrator of eastern Yong.

sentences.zh: 子直性節儉，有幹能。

translations.literal: Zizhi by nature was frugal and abstemious and had administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi was frugal by nature and capable in affairs.

sentences.zh: 魏正光中，州辟主簿，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Wei Zhengguang era the province recruited him as chief clerk; he first took office as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei Zhengguang the province made him chief clerk, and he entered service as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 永安初，拜鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was appointed vice director of the chamberlain for dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yong'an he was made vice director of the chamberlain for dependencies.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，封山北縣男。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Shanbei county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved the capital west, he was enfeoffed baron of Shanbei.

sentences.zh: 大統初，漢熾屠各阻兵于南山，與隴東屠各共為脣齒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong the Han-chi Tuge took up arms in the Southern Mountains, allied with the Longdong Tuge as mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong the Han-chi Tuge rebels held the Southern Mountains, allied with the Longdong Tuge as mutual support.

sentences.zh: 周文帝令子直率涇州步騎五千討破之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai ordered Zizhi to lead five thousand infantry and cavalry from Jing Province to attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai ordered Zizhi to lead five thousand foot and horse from Jing Province against them and break the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賜書勞問，除尚書左外兵郎中，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was granted a letter of commendation and inquiry, appointed outer troops gentleman of the left in the Masters of Writing, and concurrently secretariat aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai sent a letter of commendation, then appointed him outer troops gentleman of the left in the masters of writing and concurrent secretariat aide.

sentences.zh: 從解洛陽圍，經河橋戰，兼尚書左丞，出為秦總管府司馬。

translations.literal: He followed in lifting the siege of Luoyang, fought at Heqiao, served concurrently as left assistant director of the Masters of Writing, and was sent out as marshal of the Qin headquarters command.
translations.idiomatic: He helped lift the siege of Luoyang, fought at Heqiao, served concurrently as left assistant director of the masters of writing, and was sent out as marshal of the Qin headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時涼州刺史宇文仲和據州逆命，子直從隴右大都督獨孤信討平之。

translations.literal: At the time Governor of Liang Province Yuwen Zhonghe held the province in defiance of orders; Zizhi followed Longyou area commander Dugu Xin to attack and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Province governor Yuwen Zhonghe rebelled and held the province, Zizhi followed Longyou area commander Dugu Xin and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 復入為大行台郎中，兼丞相府記室，除太子中庶子，領齊王友。

translations.literal: He again entered service as gentleman of the great mobile headquarters and recording secretary of the chancellor's office, was appointed junior tutor to the crown prince, and served as companion to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as gentleman of the great mobile headquarters and recording secretary on the chancellor's staff, was appointed junior tutor to the crown prince, and served as companion to the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 尋行馮翊郡事。

translations.literal: Soon he governed Fengyi commandery in an acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he governed Fengyi commandery in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元年，拜使持節、大都督，行瓜州事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Fei he was appointed bearer of the staff of authority and great area commander, governing Gua Province in an acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei he was made bearer of the staff of authority and great area commander, governing Gua Province in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 務以德政化人，西土悅附。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to governing the people through virtuous policy; the western lands gladly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to civilize the people through virtuous government, and the western regions gladly followed him.

sentences.zh: 恭帝初，徵拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gong he was summoned and appointed gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Gong's reign he was summoned and made gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子宣禮，柱國府參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xuanli served as staff officer in the office of a pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanli served as staff officer in a pillar-general's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 杜杲，字子暉，京兆杜陵人也，祖建，魏輔國將軍，贈蒙州刺史。

translations.literal: Du Guo, courtesy name Zihui, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao. His grandfather Jian was a general who supports the state in Wei, posthumously awarded as governor of Meng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guo, courtesy name Zihui, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao. His grandfather Jian had been a general who supports the state under Wei and was posthumously made governor of Meng Province.

sentences.zh: 父皎，儀同三司、武都郡守。

translations.literal: His father Jiao held the rank of Commissioner with Same Privileges as the Three Departments and was governor of Wudu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiao held the rank of commissioner with privileges equal to the Three Departments and served as governor of Wudu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 杲學涉經史，有當世幹略，其族父攢，清貞有識鑒，深器重之，常曰：「吾家千里駒也。」

translations.literal: Guo was broadly learned in the classics and histories and possessed contemporary strategic ability. His clansman Zan, pure and perceptive, held him in deep esteem and often said: "The fine steed of our house."
translations.idiomatic: Guo was broadly versed in the classics and histories and possessed real talent for affairs of the day. His clansman Zan, upright and discerning, thought very highly of him and often said: "Here is the thousand-li colt of our clan."

sentences.zh: 攢時仕魏，為黃門侍郎，兼度支尚書、衛大將軍、西道大行台，尚孝武妹新豐公主，因薦之朝廷。

translations.literal: Zan was then serving Wei as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, concurrently Minister of Revenue, General of the Guard, and Grand Commissioner of the Western Circuit; he had married Emperor Xiaowu's sister, Princess Xinfeng, and through this recommended him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was then in Wei service as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, concurrently Minister of Revenue, General of the Guard, and Grand Commissioner of the Western Circuit; married to Emperor Xiaowu's sister, Princess Xinfeng, he recommended Guo to the court.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, he began his career as a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi (533), he entered service as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 周明帝初，為脩城郡守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Zhou, he was governor of Xiucheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Ming of Northern Zhou, he was appointed governor of Xiucheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 屬鳳州人仇周貢等構亂，攻逼脩城，杲信洽於人，部內遂無叛者。

translations.literal: When people of Fengzhou including Qiu Zhougong stirred up disorder and pressed the attack on Xiucheng, Guo's credibility won over the people, and within his jurisdiction there were no defectors.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu Zhougong and others of Fengzhou raised a rebellion and pressed the siege of Xiucheng, Guo's trust among the people was so complete that no one in his district joined the rebels.

sentences.zh: 尋率郡兵與開府趙昶合勢，並破平之。

translations.literal: Soon he led the commandery troops to join forces with Zhao Chang, commissioner with independent command, and together they crushed and pacified the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he led the commandery troops to join Commissioner Zhao Chang, and together they routed the rebels and restored order.

sentences.zh: 入為司會上士。

translations.literal: He entered service as senior officer of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed senior officer in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 初，陳文帝弟安成王頊為質于梁，及江陵平，頊隨例遷長安。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wen of Chen's younger brother, Prince An Cheng Xu, had been a hostage in Liang; when Jiangling fell, Xu was transferred to Chang'an along with the others.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chen Emperor Wen's younger brother, Prince Xu of Ancheng, had been held as a hostage in Liang; when Jiangling fell, Xu was moved to Chang'an with the other captives.

sentences.zh: 陳人請之，周文帝許而未遣。

translations.literal: The Chen side requested his return; Emperor Wen of Zhou agreed but did not yet send him back.
translations.idiomatic: Chen asked for his return; Northern Zhou Emperor Wen agreed in principle but did not yet release him.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝欲歸之，命杲使焉。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor wished to return him and ordered Guo to go as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion the emperor decided to send Xu home and dispatched Guo as envoy.

sentences.zh: 陳文帝大悅，即遣使報聘，並賂黔中數州地，仍請畫野分疆，永敦鄰好。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Chen was greatly pleased, immediately sent envoys in return, ceded several prefectures in Qianzhong as a gift, and further requested demarcation of borders to cement neighborly friendship forever.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Emperor Wen was delighted, promptly sent envoys in return, offered several prefectures in Qianzhong as a gift, and asked that borders be drawn so that good relations might endure.

sentences.zh: 以杲奉使稱旨，進授都督，行小禦伯，更往分界。

translations.literal: Because Guo's mission accorded with the imperial intent, he was promoted to regional commander and acting Junior Defender Baron, and sent again to demarcate the border.
translations.idiomatic: Because Guo's embassy had fully satisfied the throne, he was promoted to regional commander and acting Junior Defender Baron and sent back to settle the frontier.

sentences.zh: 陳於是歸魯山郡。

translations.literal: Chen thereupon returned Lushan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen thereupon restored Lushan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝乃拜頊柱國大將軍，詔杲送之還國。

translations.literal: The emperor then enfeoffed Xu as Pillar General and ordered Guo to escort him back to his country.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor then enfeoffed Xu as Pillar General and ordered Guo to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 陳文帝謂杲曰：「家弟今蒙禮遣，實是周朝之惠。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Chen said to Guo: "My younger brother has now received the courtesy of being sent home—this is truly a kindness from the Zhou court.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Emperor Wen said to Guo: "My brother has now been honorably sent home—a genuine kindness from your court.

sentences.zh: 然不還魯山，亦恐未能及此。」

translations.literal: Yet had Lushan not been returned, I fear this might not have been possible."
translations.idiomatic: Yet had Lushan not been returned, I doubt this would have been possible".

sentences.zh: 杲答曰：「安成之在關中，乃咸陽一布衣耳。

translations.literal: Guo replied: "When Prince An Cheng was in the Guanzhong region, he was no more than a common cloth-clad man of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo replied: "When Prince Xu of Ancheng was in Guanzhong, he was no more than a commoner of Xianyang in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 然是陳之介弟，其價豈止一城？

translations.literal: Yet he is Chen's honored younger brother—is his worth limited to a single city?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he is Chen's own brother—is his worth no more than one walled town?

sentences.zh: 本朝親睦九族，恕己及物，上遵太祖遺旨，下思繼好之義，所以發德音者，蓋為此也。

translations.literal: Our court cherishes the nine degrees of kinship, extends forbearance from oneself to others, above observes the founding emperor's testament, below honors the duty of continuing friendly relations—the reason for issuing this gracious decree is precisely this.
translations.idiomatic: Our court cherishes kinship through the nine degrees of relation, extends forbearance from oneself to others, honors above the founding emperor's testament and below the duty of lasting friendship—that is why this gracious decree was issued.

sentences.zh: 若知止侔魯山，固當不貪一鎮。

translations.literal: If Prince Xu were worth no more than Lushan, we would certainly not be greedy for one commandery.
translations.idiomatic: If Prince Xu were worth no more than Lushan, we would certainly not covet a single commandery.

sentences.zh: 況魯山梁之舊地，梁即本朝籓臣，若以始末言之，魯山自合歸國。

translations.literal: Moreover Lushan was Liang's former territory, and Liang was itself our court's vassal—in light of the whole history, Lushan ought by rights to return to our state.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Lushan was former Liang territory, and Liang was itself our court's vassal; judged by the whole course of events, Lushan ought by rights to have returned to us.

sentences.zh: 雲以尋常之土，易已骨肉之親，使臣猶謂不可，何以聞諸朝廷！」

translations.literal: To speak of trading ordinary land for one's own kin—even your envoy finds it impossible; how could I report such a thing to our court!"
translations.idiomatic: To propose trading ordinary soil for one's own flesh and blood—even I find that impossible; how could I report such a thing to my court"!

sentences.zh: 陳文帝慚恧久之，乃曰：「前言戲之耳！」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Chen was ashamed for a long while, then said: "My earlier words were spoken in jest!"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Emperor Wen was abashed for some time, then said: "What I said before was only in jest"!

sentences.zh: 自是接遇有加常禮。

translations.literal: From then on he received Guo with honors beyond the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he treated Guo with honors beyond the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 及還，引升殿，親降御座，執手以別。

translations.literal: When Guo was about to return, the emperor led him up to the hall, personally descended from the imperial seat, and clasped his hand in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo was leaving, the emperor led him into the hall, came down from the throne in person, and clasped his hand in farewell.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，授大都督、小載師下大夫，行小納言，復聘于陳。

translations.literal: The Zhou court commended him, appointing him Grand Regional Commander, junior grand master under the Master of Carriages, acting Junior Remonstrator, and sent him on another mission to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou court commended him, appointing him Grand Regional Commander, junior grand master under the Master of Carriages, and acting Junior Remonstrator, and sent him on another embassy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 及華皎來附，詔令衛公直、都督元定等援之。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao came over to submit, an edict ordered Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi, regional commander Yuan Ding, and others to support him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao defected to Zhou, an edict ordered Duke Yuwen Zhi of Wei, Regional Commander Yuan Ding, and others to go to his aid.

sentences.zh: 定等並沒。

translations.literal: Ding and the others were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Ding and his men were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 自是連兵不息，東南搔動。

translations.literal: From then on fighting continued without pause and the southeast was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the fighting never let up, and the southeast was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 武帝授杲禦正中大夫，使陳，論保境息人之意。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu appointed Guo Chief Straightening Grand Master and sent him to Chen to discuss the idea of securing borders and giving the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu appointed Guo Chief Straightening Grand Master and sent him to Chen to propose securing the borders and giving the people peace.

sentences.zh: 陳宣帝遣其黃門侍郎徐陵謂杲曰：「兩國通好，彼朝受我叛人，何也？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen sent his Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Xu Ling to say to Guo: "Our two states are on friendly terms—why does your court accept our defectors?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Emperor Xuan sent his Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Xu Ling, to say to Guo: "Our two states are at peace—why does your court take in our deserters"?

sentences.zh: 杲曰：「陳主昔在本朝，非慕義而至，主上授以柱國，位極人臣，子女玉帛，備禮將送，今主社稷，孰謂非恩？

translations.literal: Guo said: "The Chen ruler once dwelt in our court—not because he admired our righteousness did he come; our sovereign enfeoffed him as Pillar of State, raised him to the utmost rank, and sent him off with full ceremony of sons, daughters, jade, and silks. Now he rules his realm—who would say this is not grace?
translations.idiomatic: Guo said: "Your ruler once lived at our court—not because he admired our righteousness; our sovereign made him a Pillar of State, raised him to the highest rank, and sent him home with sons, daughters, jade, and silks in full ceremony. Now he sits upon the Chen throne—who would call that anything but grace?

sentences.zh: 郝烈之徒，邊人狂狡，曾未報德，而先納之。

translations.literal: The likes of Hao Lie were wild and cunning border folk who had never repaid kindness, yet you took them in first.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Hao Lie were wild, cunning border folk who had never repaid a kindness, yet you took them in first.

sentences.zh: 今受華氏，正是相報。

translations.literal: Now that we accept the Hua clan, it is precisely repayment in kind.
translations.idiomatic: Our acceptance of the Hua clan is simply repayment in kind.

sentences.zh: 過自彼始，豈在本朝！」

translations.literal: The offense began on your side—how can it be laid at our court's door!"
translations.idiomatic: The offense began on your side—how can the fault be ours"!

sentences.zh: 陵曰：「彼納華皎，志圖吞噬。

translations.literal: Ling said: "In accepting Hua Jiao, your side aims at swallowing us whole.
translations.idiomatic: Ling said: "In taking Hua Jiao, your court aims at swallowing us whole.

sentences.zh: 此受郝烈。

translations.literal: In this matter we accepted Hao Lie.
translations.idiomatic: In this case we took in Hao Lie.

sentences.zh: 容之而已。

translations.literal: We merely harbored him, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: We merely gave him shelter—that is all.

sentences.zh: 且華皎方州列將。

translations.literal: Moreover Hua Jiao was a regional commander and ranked general.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Hua Jiao was a frontier commander and a ranked general.

sentences.zh: 竊邑叛亡。

translations.literal: He seized a city and rebelled in flight.
translations.idiomatic: He seized his command and fled in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 郝烈一百許戶，脫身逃竄。

translations.literal: Hao Lie was a mere hundred or so households who slipped away in escape.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Lie was no more than a hundred-odd households who slipped away in flight.

sentences.zh: 大小有異，豈得同年而語乎？」

translations.literal: The scale differs—how can they be spoken of in the same breath?"
translations.idiomatic: The cases differ in scale—how can they be mentioned in the same breath"?

sentences.zh: 杲曰：「大小雖殊，受降一也。

translations.literal: Guo said: "Though the scale differs, accepting surrender is the same principle.
translations.idiomatic: Guo said: "Great or small, the principle of accepting surrender is the same.

sentences.zh: 若論先後，本朝無失。」

translations.literal: If we speak of sequence, our court was not in the wrong."
translations.idiomatic: If we speak of who acted first, our court was not in the wrong".

sentences.zh: 陵曰：「周朝送主上還國，既以為恩，衛公共元定度江，孰云非怨？

translations.literal: Ling said: "Your Zhou court sent our ruler home—you call that kindness; Duke of Wei and Yuan Ding crossed the Yangtze—is that not grounds for grievance?
translations.idiomatic: Ling said: "Your Zhou court sent our ruler home and call that kindness; Duke Yuwen Zhi of Wei and Yuan Ding crossed the Yangtze—is that not cause for grievance?

sentences.zh: 計恩與怨，亦足相埒。」

translations.literal: Counting kindness against grievance, they are sufficient to balance each other."
translations.idiomatic: Set kindness against grievance, and the two are enough to cancel each other out".

sentences.zh: 杲曰：「元定等軍敗身囚，其怨已滅。

translations.literal: Guo said: "Yuan Ding and the others were defeated and taken captive—their grievance is already extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Guo said: "Yuan Ding and his men were defeated and taken prisoner—the grievance from that is already spent.

sentences.zh: 陳主負扆馮玉，其恩猶在。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler sits upon the throne with jade before him—your grace still stands.
translations.idiomatic: Your ruler sits upon the throne with the jade screen before him—the grace you received still stands.

sentences.zh: 且怨由彼國，恩起本朝，以怨酬恩，未之聞也。」

translations.literal: Moreover the grievance arose from your state and the grace from ours—to repay grace with grievance—is unheard of."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the grievance came from your state and the grace from ours—to answer grace with grievance is something I have never heard of".

sentences.zh: 陵笑而不答。

translations.literal: Ling smiled and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Ling smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 杲因陳和通之便，陵具以聞。

translations.literal: Guo took advantage of the opportunity to discuss peace, and Ling reported everything to his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing the opening to discuss peace, Guo pressed his case, and Ling reported the whole exchange to his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 陳宣許之，遂遣使來聘。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen agreed and thereupon sent envoys to pay a court visit.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Emperor Xuan agreed and thereupon sent envoys on a formal visit.

sentences.zh: 建德初，授司城中大夫，仍使于陳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, he was appointed Grand Master of the City Guard and again sent as envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jiande era (572), he was made Grand Master of the City Guard and again dispatched to Chen.

sentences.zh: 宣帝謂杲曰：「長湖公軍人等雖築館處之，然恐不能無北風之戀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan said to Guo: "Although Changhu Duke's soldiers and the like are housed in lodges, I fear they cannot be without longing for the northern wind.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan said to Guo: "Although Duke Changhu's soldiers and the like are lodged in comfort, I fear they cannot be without longing for the northern wind.

sentences.zh: 王褒、庾信之徒既羈旅關中，亦當有南枝之思耳。」

translations.literal: Wang Bao, Yu Xin, and their fellows, detained in the Guanzhong, must also have thoughts of the southern branch."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao, Yu Xin, and their fellows, living as exiles in Guanzhong, must likewise yearn for the southern branch".

sentences.zh: 杲揣陳宣意欲以元定軍將士易王褒等，乃答之曰：「長湖總戎失律，臨雖苟免，既不死節，安用此為！

translations.literal: Guo inferred that Emperor Xuan wished to exchange Yuan Ding's army officers and men for Wang Bao and the others, and answered: "Changhu led the army in violation of discipline; though he narrowly escaped at the end, since he did not die loyal to duty, what use is he!
translations.idiomatic: Guo guessed that Emperor Xuan meant to trade Yuan Ding's captured officers and men for Wang Bao and the others, and answered: "Duke Changhu lost command of his army; though he narrowly escaped with his life, since he did not die in loyal service, of what use is he!

sentences.zh: 且猶牛之一毛，何能損益。

translations.literal: Moreover they are but one hair from an ox's hide—what gain or loss could they make?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, they are but one hair from an ox's hide—what difference could they make either way?

sentences.zh: 本朝之議，初未及此。」

translations.literal: Our court's deliberations never extended to this."
translations.idiomatic: Our court's deliberations never touched on any such exchange".

sentences.zh: 陳宣帝乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Emperor Xuan then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 及杲還，至石頭，又遣謂之曰：「若欲合從，共圖齊氏，能以樊、鄧見與，方可表信。」

translations.literal: When Guo was returning and reached Shitou, the Chen side again sent word saying: "If you wish to ally together and jointly plot against the Qi, you must cede Fan and Deng to us before we can show good faith."
translations.idiomatic: When Guo was on his way back and reached Shitou, Chen again sent word saying: "If you wish to ally and jointly move against Qi, you must give us Fan and Deng before we can show good faith".

sentences.zh: 杲答曰：「合從圖齊，豈唯弊邑之利？

translations.literal: Guo replied: "To ally and plot against Qi—would that benefit only our humble state?
translations.idiomatic: Guo answered: "An alliance to move against Qi would benefit more than our state alone—

sentences.zh: 必須城鎮，宜待得之于齊。

translations.literal: If fortified towns are required, it is fitting to wait until they are taken from Qi.
translations.idiomatic: if you insist on fortified towns, wait until they are taken from Qi.

sentences.zh: 先索漢南，使臣不敢聞命。」

translations.literal: To demand Han-nan first makes your envoy dare not accept the commission."
translations.idiomatic: To demand Han-nan first leaves your envoy no choice but to refuse the commission".

sentences.zh: 還，除司倉中大夫，又使于陳。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Grand Master of the Granary and again sent as envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Grand Master of the Granary and again dispatched to Chen.

sentences.zh: 杲有辭辯，閑於占對，前後將命，陳人不能屈，陳宣帝甚敬異之。

translations.literal: Guo had eloquence and skill in debate; in successive missions the men of Chen could not best him, and Emperor Xuan of Chen held him in great respect and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Guo was eloquent and quick in repartee; mission after mission, the Chen envoys could not get the better of him, and Chen Emperor Xuan came to admire him greatly.

sentences.zh: 時元定已卒，乃禮送開府賀拔華及定棺樞，杲受之以歸。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Ding had already died; Chen then ceremonially sent back the staff of Heba Hua, who had opened a headquarters, together with Ding's coffin and bier, and Guo received them and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuan Ding was already dead; Chen ceremonially sent back the staff of headquarters commander Heba Hua together with Ding's coffin and bier, and Guo received them and brought them home.

sentences.zh: 除河東郡守，遷溫州刺史，賜爵義興縣伯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Hedong Commandery, promoted to Governor of Wen Province, and enfeoffed as Baron of Yixing County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Administrator of Hedong Commandery, then promoted to Governor of Wen Province and enfeoffed as Baron of Yixing County.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，徵拜禦正中大夫，復使陳。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daxiang, he was summoned and appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Rectitude and again sent to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daxiang (579), he was summoned to court as Grand Master of the Imperial Rectitude and again sent to Chen.

sentences.zh: 二年，除申州刺史，加開府儀同大將軍，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Governor of Shen Province, given the rank of Grand Master of the Headquarters with ceremonial parity to a great general, and advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Governor of Shen Province, granted the rank of Grand Master of the Headquarters with ceremonial parity to a great general, and raised to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 除同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇元年，以杲為同州總管，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang of Sui, Guo was made overall commander of Tong Province and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang (581), Guo was made overall commander of Tong Province and raised to Duke.

sentences.zh: 俄遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二年，除西南道行台兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Minister of the Bureau of Military Affairs on the Southwestern Circuit Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Minister of the Bureau of Military Affairs on the Southwestern Circuit Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子運，大象末，宣納上士。

translations.literal: His son Yun, at the end of the Daxiang era, held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary for Presentation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun, at the end of the Daxiang era, served as Attendant-in-Ordinary for Presentation.

sentences.zh: 杲兄長暉，位儀同三司。

translations.literal: Guo's elder brother Changhui held the third rank of ceremonial parity.
translations.idiomatic: Guo's elder brother Changhui held the third rank of ceremonial parity.

sentences.zh: 呂思禮，東平壽張人也。

translations.literal: Lu Sili was a native of Shouzhang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sili came from Shouzhang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 性溫潤，不雜交遊。

translations.literal: By nature he was gentle and mild and did not mix in social intercourse.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and even-tempered by nature, he kept to himself and rarely mingled in society.

sentences.zh: 年十四，受學于徐遵明，長於論難，諸生為之語曰：「講《書》論《易》鋒難敵。」

translations.literal: At fourteen he studied under Xu Zunming; he excelled in disputation, and the students said of him: "When lecturing on the Book of Documents and debating the Book of Changes, none can match the edge of his challenge."
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he studied under Xu Zunming and excelled in debate; the students said of him: "When he lectures on the Documents and disputes over the Changes, no one can stand against his thrust".

sentences.zh: 十九，舉秀才，對策高第，除相州功曹參軍。

translations.literal: At nineteen he was nominated as a xiucai, placed at the top of the policy examination, and appointed Army Aide of Merit in Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he was nominated as a xiucai, ranked first in the policy examination, and appointed Army Aide of Merit in Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 葛榮圍鄴，思禮有守禦勳，賜爵平陵縣伯，除欒城令。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong besieged Ye, Sili had merit in the defense; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingling County and appointed Magistrate of Luancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong besieged Ye, Sili won distinction in the defense; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingling County and made Magistrate of Luancheng.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，僕射司馬子如薦為尚書二千石郎中。

translations.literal: In the Putai era, Vice Director Sima Ziru recommended him as Langzhong in the Ministry of the Two Thousand Bushels.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putai era, Vice Director Sima Ziru recommended him for the post of Langzhong in the Ministry of the Two Thousand Bushels.

sentences.zh: 尋以地寒被出，兼國子博士。

translations.literal: Before long, because of his humble origins he was dismissed and concurrently appointed Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed on account of his low birth and concurrently appointed Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 乃求為關西大行台郎中，與姚幼瑜、茹文就俱入關。

translations.literal: He then requested appointment as Langzhong on the Great Western Circuit Headquarters and entered the Pass together with Yao Youyu and Ru Wenjiu.
translations.idiomatic: He then sought appointment as Langzhong on the Great Western Circuit Headquarters and entered the Pass with Yao Youyu and Ru Wenjiu.

sentences.zh: 為行台賀拔嶽所重，專掌機密，甚得時譽。

translations.literal: He was valued by Heba Yue of the Circuit Headquarters, was put in sole charge of confidential affairs, and won great contemporary renown.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue of the circuit headquarters prized him, entrusted him with confidential affairs alone, and he won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 岳為侯莫陳悅所害，趙貴等議遣赫連達迎周文帝，思禮預其謀。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed by Hou Mo Chen Yue, Zhao Gui and the others deliberated sending Helian Da to welcome the Duke of Zhou; Sili took part in the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was murdered by Hou Mo Chen Yue, Zhao Gui and the others planned to send Helian Da to welcome the Duke of Zhou, and Sili joined the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 及周文為關西大都督，以思禮為府長史，尋除行台右丞。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Zhou became Grand Commander of the Western Pass, he appointed Sili Chief Clerk of his headquarters and soon afterward made him Right Assistant Director of the Circuit Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Zhou became Grand Commander of the Western Pass, he made Sili Chief Clerk of his headquarters and soon afterward Right Assistant Director of the Circuit Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 以迎魏孝武功，封汶陽縣子，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: For the merit of welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wenyang and given the rank of General Who Conquers the Enemy.
translations.idiomatic: For escorting Emperor Xiaowu of Wei to safety, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wenyang and made General Who Conquers the Enemy.

sentences.zh: 拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝即位，領著作郎，除安東將軍、都官尚書，兼七兵、殿中二曹事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Wei acceded, he served as Director of the Bureau of Compilation, was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Minister of Punishments, and concurrently oversaw the two bureaus of the Seven Armies and the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei acceded, he served as Director of the Bureau of Compilation, was made General Who Pacifies the East and Minister of Punishments, and concurrently oversaw the bureaus of the Seven Armies and the Palace.

sentences.zh: 從禽竇泰，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Dou Tai, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Tai was taken captive, he was raised to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，以謗訕朝政賜死。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong, he was sentenced to death for slandering the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong (538), he was executed for slandering the court.

sentences.zh: 思禮好學有才，雖務兼軍國，而手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Sili loved learning and had talent; though his duties combined military and state affairs, he never put his books aside.
translations.idiomatic: Sili loved learning and was gifted; though he shouldered both military and civil duties, he never let his books out of his hands.

sentences.zh: 晝理政事，夜即讀書，令蒼頭執燭，燭燼夜有數升。

translations.literal: By day he handled government; at night he read, having a servant hold the candle—when the night was done, the spent tallow amounted to several sheng.
translations.idiomatic: By day he governed; at night he read, with a servant holding the candle—by morning the melted tallow filled several sheng.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之捷，命為露布，食頃便成，周文歎其工而且速。

translations.literal: After the victory at Shachuan, he was ordered to draft the victory bulletin; in the time it takes to eat a meal it was finished, and the Duke of Zhou marveled at its craftsmanship and speed.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Shachuan he was ordered to draft the victory bulletin; he finished it in the time it takes to eat a meal, and the Duke of Zhou marveled at its polish and speed.

sentences.zh: 所為碑誄表頌，並傳於世。

translations.literal: The stele inscriptions, dirges, memorials, and eulogies he wrote all circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: The stele inscriptions, dirges, memorials, and eulogies he wrote all passed into circulation.

sentences.zh: 七年，追贈車騎將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was posthumously appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was posthumously made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子亶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Dan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 大象中，位至駕部下大夫。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era he rose to Grand Master under the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daxiang era he rose to Grand Master under the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 時有博陵崔騰，早有名譽，曆職清顯，為丞相府長史，亦以投書謗議賜死。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Teng of Boling, who had long enjoyed a fine reputation and held successive posts of clear distinction, serving as Chief Clerk of the Chancellor's Headquarters, was likewise sentenced to death for sending letters of slander and criticism.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cui Teng of Boling, long celebrated and repeatedly promoted to distinguished posts, who served as Chief Clerk of the Chancellor's Headquarters, was likewise executed for circulating letters of slander and criticism.

sentences.zh: 徐招，字思賢，高平金鄉人也。

translations.literal: Xu Zhao, style name Sixian, was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhao, whose style name was Sixian, came from Jinxiang in Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 世為著姓。

translations.literal: His family had been a prominent clan for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been a prominent clan for generations.

sentences.zh: 招少好法律及朝廷舊事，發言措筆，常欲辯析秋毫，初入洛陽，雖未登仕，已為時知，朝廷疑事多預議焉。

translations.literal: From youth Zhao loved law and the old precedents of the court; in speech and in writing he always sought to parse distinctions finer than an autumn hair. When he first entered Luoyang, though he had not yet taken office, he was already known to the age, and on doubtful matters the court often consulted him beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhao loved law and the court's ancient precedents; in speech and writing he always strove to split hairs finer than an autumn hair. When he first came to Luoyang, though he had not yet entered office, he was already known in the capital, and the court often sought his opinion on doubtful matters.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，從征浮山堰有功，賜爵高文男。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era, he followed the campaign against the Fushan Dam and had merit; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaowen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanchang era he took part in the campaign against the Fushan Dam and won distinction; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaowen.

sentences.zh: 及廣陽王深北討鮮于脩禮，啟為員外散騎侍郎、深府長流參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Guangyang led the northern expedition against Xianyu Xiuli, Zhao was recommended as Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chief Aide of the prince's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Guangyang marched north against Xianyu Xiuli, Zhao was recommended as Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chief Aide on the prince's staff.

sentences.zh: 招陳策請離間之，葛榮竟殺脩理，自為魁帥。

translations.literal: Zhao proposed a stratagem to sow discord; Ge Rong ended by killing Xiuli and made himself the chief leader.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao proposed a stratagem to set them at odds; Ge Rong ended by killing Xiuli and proclaimed himself chief leader.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為侯。

translations.literal: For this merit he was advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was raised to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 永安初，射策甲科，除員外散騎常侍，領尚書儀曹郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he placed first in the archery examination, was appointed Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary, and served as Langzhong in the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yong'an he placed first in the archery examination, was made Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary, and served as Langzhong in the Ministry of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 招少習吏事，未能精究朝儀，常恨才達，恐名跡不立。

translations.literal: Zhao had studied clerical work from youth and had not yet mastered court ritual in full; he always regretted that his talent had outrun his learning and feared his name and record would not stand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had trained in clerical work from youth and had not yet mastered court ritual in full; he always feared that talent had outpaced learning and that his name would not endure.

sentences.zh: 久之，方轉二千石郎中。

translations.literal: After a long time he was finally transferred to Langzhong in the Ministry of the Two Thousand Bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long delay was he transferred to Langzhong in the Ministry of the Two Thousand Bushels.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮死，爾硃世隆屯兵河橋，莊帝以招為行台左丞，自武牢北度，引馬場、河內之眾以抗世隆。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Erzhu Shilong encamped his troops at Heqiao; Emperor Zhuang appointed Zhao Left Assistant Director of the Circuit Headquarters, and he crossed north from Wulao, leading the forces of Machang and Henei to resist Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Erzhu Shilong encamped at Heqiao; Emperor Zhuang appointed Zhao Left Assistant Director of the Circuit Headquarters, and he crossed north from Wulao at the head of the forces of Machang and Henei to resist Shilong.

sentences.zh: 後爾硃兆得招，鎖送洛陽，仲遠數招罪，將斬之。

translations.literal: Later Erzhu Zhao captured Zhao, bound him, and sent him to Luoyang; Zhongyuan listed Zhao's crimes and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Erzhu Zhao captured Zhao, bound him, and sent him to Luoyang; Zhongyuan recited his crimes and was about to behead him.

sentences.zh: 招曰：「不虧君命，得死為幸。」

translations.literal: Zhao said: "I have not failed my lord's commission; to die is my good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said: "I have not betrayed my lord's commission—to die would be my good fortune".

sentences.zh: 仲遠重之，曰：「凡人受命，理各為主。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan respected him and said: "When any man receives a commission, reason demands that each serve his own master.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan respected him and said: "Every man who receives a commission is bound to serve his own master.

sentences.zh: 今若為戮，何以勸人臣？」

translations.literal: If he is now put to death, how can other ministers be encouraged?"
translations.idiomatic: If we execute him now, what encouragement is that to other ministers"?

sentences.zh: 乃釋之，用為行台右丞。

translations.literal: He thereupon released him and employed him as Right Assistant Director of the Circuit Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon released him and appointed him Right Assistant Director of the Circuit Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及仲遠南奔，招獨還洛。

translations.literal: When Zhongyuan fled south, Zhao alone returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongyuan fled south, Zhao alone returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 永熙末，從孝武入關中，拜給事黃門侍郎，兼尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongxi he followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong and was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary in the Service of Affairs and concurrently Assistant Director of the Right in the Ministry of State.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongxi he followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong and was made Attendant-in-Ordinary in the Service of Affairs and concurrently Assistant Director of the Right in the Ministry of State.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷播遷，典章遺闕，至於台省法式，皆招所記，論者多焉。

translations.literal: At that time the court was in flight and statutes were lost; as for the forms and rules of the ministries and inspectorates, all were recorded by Zhao, and many were the men who debated them.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then in exile and its statutes in disarray; the forms and rules of the ministries and inspectorates were largely Zhao's record, and many men drew on his work.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，拜驃騎將軍、侍中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong (537) he was made General of Agile Cavalry and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時文帝舅子王起化犯罪死，有詔追贈，招執奏正之。

translations.literal: At that time the maternal nephew of Emperor Wen, Wang Qihua, had been executed for a crime; an edict ordered posthumous honors, but Zhao submitted a memorial correcting the error.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Wen's nephew by marriage, Wang Qihua, had been executed for a crime; an edict ordered posthumous honors, but Zhao memorialized the throne and corrected the mistake.

sentences.zh: 後卒于度支尚書。

translations.literal: Later he died while serving as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子山雲嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shanyun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shanyun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 檀翥，字鳳翔，高平金鄉人也。

translations.literal: Tan Zhu, style name Fengxiang, was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhu, whose style name was Fengxiang, came from Jinxiang in Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 六世祖毓，晉步兵校尉。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Yu was Infantry Commandant of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Yu had been Infantry Commandant under Jin.

sentences.zh: 父江，始還北，仁至太常少卿，贈兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jiang, when he first returned north, rose as far as Vice Minister of Ceremonies and was posthumously appointed Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiang, after first returning to the north, rose as far as Vice Minister of Ceremonies and was posthumously made Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 翥十歲喪父，還京師宅，與營人雜居。

translations.literal: Zhu lost his father at ten, returned to the family house in the capital, and lived mixed among laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu lost his father at ten, returned to the family house in the capital, and lived among the laborers who camped there.

sentences.zh: 雖幼孤寒，不與鄰人來往。

translations.literal: Though young, orphaned, and poor, he did not mingle with his neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a boy, orphaned, and poor, he kept apart from his neighbors.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，解屬文，能鼓琴，早為琅邪王誦所知。

translations.literal: He loved reading, could compose linked prose, knew how to play the zither, and from early on was known to Prince Song of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books, could write linked prose, played the zither, and from early on won the notice of the Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 年十九，以名家子為魏明帝挽郎。

translations.literal: At nineteen, as the son of an eminent house, he served as a mourning attendant for Emperor Ming of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen, as the son of an eminent house, he served as a mourning attendant at the funeral of Emperor Ming of Wei.

sentences.zh: 後客游三輔，時毛遐為行台，鎮北雍，表翥為行台郎中。

translations.literal: Later, traveling as a guest in the Three Metropolises, at that time Mao Xia held a circuit headquarters and guarded northern Yong; he memorialized that Zhu be appointed Langzhong on the headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while traveling as a guest in the Three Metropolises, he came to the notice of Mao Xia, who held a circuit headquarters and guarded northern Yong; Xia memorialized that Zhu be made Langzhong on his staff.

sentences.zh: 莊帝既誅爾硃榮，遐使翥詣亦師，因除著作佐郎，郎中如故。

translations.literal: After Emperor Zhuang had executed Erzhu Rong, Xia sent Zhu to the capital, and he was appointed Assistant Director in the Bureau of Compilation while retaining his post as Langzhong.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhuang executed Erzhu Rong, Xia sent Zhu to the capital, where he was appointed Assistant Director in the Bureau of Compilation while retaining his post as Langzhong.

sentences.zh: 後孝武帝西幸，除兼中書舍人，修國史。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Xiaowu went west, Zhu was appointed Supernumerary Secretariat Attendant and charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Zhu was made Supernumerary Secretariat Attendant and charged with compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 大統初，又兼著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he again concurrently served as Assistant Director in the Bureau of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong he again concurrently served as Assistant Director in the Bureau of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 以守關迎賀勳，封高唐子。

translations.literal: For the merit of guarding the pass and welcoming He, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: For guarding the pass and welcoming He, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 後坐談論輕躁，為黃門侍郎徐招所糾，死于廷尉獄。

translations.literal: Later, for reckless talk he was impeached by Attendant-in-Ordinary Xu Zhao and died in the prison of the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for reckless speech he was impeached by Attendant-in-Ordinary Xu Zhao and died in the prison of the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 孟信，字脩仁，廣川索盧人也。

translations.literal: Meng Xin, style name Xiuren, was a native of Suolu in Guangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xin, whose style name was Xiuren, came from Suolu in Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 家世貧寒，頗傳學業。

translations.literal: His family had been poor and cold for generations, yet had passed down learning.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been poor for generations, yet had kept up its scholarly tradition.

sentences.zh: 信常曰：「窮則變，變則通。

translations.literal: Xin often said: "When cornered, one changes; when one changes, one finds a way through.
translations.idiomatic: Xin often said: "When cornered, one changes; when one changes, one finds a way through.

sentences.zh: 吾家世傳儒學，而未有通官，當由儒非世務也。」

translations.literal: Our house has transmitted Confucian learning for generations, yet none has reached high office—it must be because Confucian learning is not the business of the age."
translations.idiomatic: Our house has handed down Confucian learning for generations, yet none of us has won high office—it must be because scholarship is not the business of the age".

sentences.zh: 遂感激，棄書從軍。

translations.literal: He thereupon took fire at the words, cast aside his books, and entered the army.
translations.idiomatic: Stirred by this, he cast aside his books and took up arms.

sentences.zh: 永熙末，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongxi he was appointed Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongxi he was appointed Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 從孝武帝入關，封東州子，趙平太守。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu into the Pass, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Dongzhou, and appointed Administrator of Zhaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu into the Pass, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Dongzhou, and made Administrator of Zhaoping.

sentences.zh: 政尚寬和，權豪無犯。

translations.literal: In government he favored leniency and harmony, and the powerful did not trespass against him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was mild and conciliatory, and even the powerful did not dare cross him.

sentences.zh: 山中老人會以遥酒饋之，信和顏接引，殷勤勞問，乃自出酒，以鐵鐺溫之，素木盤盛蕪青菹，唯此而已。

translations.literal: An old man of the hills once brought him wine and cured loin as a gift; Xin received him with a gentle face, welcomed him warmly, and asked after him with care, then brought out his own wine, warmed it in an iron pot, and served it on a plain wooden tray with pickled greens—nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: An old man from the hills once brought him wine and cured loin as a gift; Xin received him kindly, welcomed him warmly, and asked after his health, then brought out his own wine, warmed it in an iron pot, and set before him only a plain wooden tray of pickled greens—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 又以一鐺借老人，但執一杯，各自斟酌，申酬酢之意，謂老人曰：「吾至郡來，無人以一物見遺，今卿獨有此餉。

translations.literal: He also lent the old man one pot; each held a single cup and poured for himself, exchanging toasts in the manner of give-and-take, and said to the old man: "Since I came to this commandery, no one has given me so much as one thing; you alone have brought me this gift.
translations.idiomatic: He also lent the old man a pot; each held a single cup and poured for himself, exchanging toasts as equals, and said: "Since I came to this commandery, no one has given me a single thing—you alone have brought me this gift.

sentences.zh: 且食菜已久，欲為卿受一遥髆耳。

translations.literal: I have eaten vegetables a long time and only wished to accept one piece of your cured loin for your sake.
translations.idiomatic: I have lived on vegetables a long time and only wished to accept one piece of your cured loin—for your sake.

sentences.zh: 酒既自有，不能相費。」

translations.literal: The wine is my own and cannot be at your expense."
translations.idiomatic: The wine is my own; I cannot let you pay for it".

sentences.zh: 老人大悅，再拜，擘遥進之。

translations.literal: The old man was greatly pleased, bowed twice, broke off the cured loin and offered it to him.
translations.idiomatic: The old man was delighted, bowed twice, broke off a piece of the cured loin, and offered it to him.

sentences.zh: 酒盡方別。

translations.literal: Only when the wine was finished did they part.
translations.idiomatic: They parted only when the wine was gone.

sentences.zh: 及去官，居貧無食。

translations.literal: When he left office he lived in poverty without food.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office he lived in poverty and had nothing to eat.

sentences.zh: 唯有一老牛，其兄子賣之，擬供薪米。

translations.literal: He had only one old ox; his elder brother's son sold it, intending to provide firewood and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He owned only one old ox; his elder brother's son sold it, intending to buy firewood and grain.

sentences.zh: 券契已訖，市法應知牛主住在所。

translations.literal: The contract was already settled; market law required that the ox's owner be known to reside on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The contract was already settled; market law required that the ox's owner be known to live on the premises.

sentences.zh: 信適從外來，見買牛人，方知其賣也。

translations.literal: Xin happened to return from outside, saw the buyer of the ox, and only then learned of the sale.
translations.idiomatic: Xin happened to return from outside, saw the man buying the ox, and only then learned it had been sold.

sentences.zh: 因告之曰：「此牛先來有病，小用便發，君不須也。」

translations.literal: He thereupon told him: "This ox was ill before; if you put it to light use it will break out again—you do not need it."
translations.idiomatic: He told the buyer: "This ox was sick before; if you put it to work it will sicken again—you do not want it".

sentences.zh: 杖其兄子二十。

translations.literal: He beat his elder brother's son twenty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: He then beat his elder brother's son twenty strokes.

sentences.zh: 買牛人嗟異良久，呼信曰：「孟公，但見與牛，未必須其力也。」

translations.literal: The buyer marveled a long while, then called to Xin and said: "Master Meng, give me the ox—I may not need its strength."
translations.idiomatic: The buyer marveled a long while, then called to Xin and said: "Master Meng, just give me the ox—I may not need its strength at all".

sentences.zh: 苦請不得，乃罷。

translations.literal: Though Xin pleaded hard, the man would not have it and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xin pressed him hard, the man would not accept and left.

sentences.zh: 買牛者，周文帝帳下人，周文深歎異焉。

translations.literal: The buyer was a man in the tent guard of Emperor Wen of Zhou; the Emperor marveled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The buyer was a man in Emperor Wen of Zhou's tent guard, and the Emperor marveled greatly at the story.

sentences.zh: 未幾，舉為太子少師，後遷太子太傅，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: Before long Xin was recommended as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince; later he was promoted to Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, to the glory of the Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recommended as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince; later he was promoted to Grand Tutor, to the glory of the scholars.

sentences.zh: 特加車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with the third rank of ceremonial parity, and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, granted the third rank of ceremonial parity, and made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 辭老請退，周文不奪其志，賜車馬、几杖、衣服、床帳。

translations.literal: He declined on account of old age and requested retirement. Emperor Wen of Zhou would not override his wish and bestowed carriages, horses, armrests, a staff, clothing, bedding, and curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his age, he asked to retire. Emperor Wen of Zhou would not deny him and sent carriages and horses, a staff and armrest, clothing, bedding, and curtains.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈冀州刺史，諡曰戴。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Governor of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Governor of Ji Province and given the posthumous title Dai.

sentences.zh: 子儒。

translations.literal: His son was Ru.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ru.

sentences.zh: 宗懍，字元懍，南陽涅陽人也。

translations.literal: Zong Lin, style name Yuanlin, was a native of Nieyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Lin, whose style name was Yuanlin, came from Nieyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 八世祖孫，永嘉亂，討陳敏有功，封柴桑縣侯，除宜都郡守。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Sun, during the chaos of the Yongjia era, achieved merit in the campaign against Chen Min and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chaisang and appointed Administrator of Yidu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eighth-generation ancestor Sun, during the chaos of the Yongjia era, won distinction in the campaign against Chen Min, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chaisang, and appointed Administrator of Yidu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子孫因居江陵。

translations.literal: His descendants therefore settled in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants thereafter made their home in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 父高之，梁山陰令。

translations.literal: His father Gaozhi was Magistrate of Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gaozhi served as Magistrate of Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 懍少聰敏，好讀書，晝夜不倦，語輒引古事，鄉里呼為「小兒學士」。

translations.literal: Lin from youth was quick-witted and loved reading, never tiring day or night. In speech he always cited ancient precedents, and the neighborhood called him the "little scholar."
translations.idiomatic: From youth Lin was quick-witted and loved books, reading day and night without fatigue. In conversation he constantly drew on ancient examples, and neighbors called him the "little scholar."

sentences.zh: 梁大同六年，舉秀才。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Datong of Liang, he was recommended as a xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Liang era Datong, he was recommended as a xiucai.

sentences.zh: 以不及二宮元會，例不對策。

translations.literal: Because he did not reach the New Year's assembly at the Two Palaces, by precedent he was not examined in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had not attended the New Year's assembly at the Two Palaces, by precedent he was not examined in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 及梁元帝鎮荊州，謂長史劉之遴曰：「貴鄉多士，為舉一有意少年。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was stationed at Jing Province, he said to Chief Clerk Liu Zhilun: "Your district has many men of talent. Recommend one promising youth for me".
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was stationed in Jing Province, he told Chief Clerk Liu Zhilun, "Your district has many talented men. Recommend one promising young man to me".

sentences.zh: 之遴以懍應命，即日引見，令兼記室。

translations.literal: Zhilun put forward Lin in response to the command, and that same day Lin was summoned for audience and appointed Acting Master of Records.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilun nominated Lin, who was summoned that very day, received an audience, and was appointed Acting Master of Records.

sentences.zh: 嘗夕被召宿省，使制《龍川廟碑》，一夜便就。

translations.literal: Once in the evening he was summoned to stay at the provincial office and ordered to compose the "Longchuan Temple Stele Inscription"; in one night it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: One evening he was summoned to remain at the provincial office and ordered to compose the "Longchuan Temple Stele Inscription"—and finished it in a single night.

sentences.zh: 詰朝呈上，梁元帝歎美之。

translations.literal: At dawn he presented it; Emperor Yuan of Liang sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he submitted it, and Emperor Yuan of Liang sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 後曆臨汝、建城、廣晉三縣令。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Magistrate of Linru, Jiancheng, and Guangjin counties.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in succession as magistrate of Linru, Jiancheng, and Guangjin counties.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂去職，哭輒歐血，兩旬之內，絕而復蘇者三。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left office. In mourning he would vomit blood; within twenty days he stopped breathing and revived three times.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office. In mourning he vomited blood so violently that within twenty days he stopped breathing and revived three times.

sentences.zh: 每旦有君烏數千集於廬舍，候哭而來，哭止而去，時論以為孝感所致。

translations.literal: Each morning several thousand lord-crows gathered at his hut, waiting for his weeping to come, and when the weeping stopped they departed. Contemporary opinion held that this was caused by filial feeling moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning thousands of crows gathered at his mourning hut, arriving when he began to weep and leaving when he stopped. People of the time took this as a sign that filial devotion had moved Heaven.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝即位，擢為尚書侍郎，封信安縣侯，累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne, Lin was promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xin'an, then repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang ascended the throne, Lin was promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xin'an, and eventually rose to Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 懍父高之先為南台書侍御史，犯憲。

translations.literal: Lin's father Gaozhi had earlier served as Attendant Censor of the Southern Secretariat and violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's father Gaozhi had earlier served as Attendant Censor of the Southern Secretariat and broken the law.

sentences.zh: 懍願父釋罪，當終身菜食。

translations.literal: Lin wished his father's crime cleared and vowed to eat only vegetables for life.
translations.idiomatic: Lin vowed that if his father's guilt were cleared he would eat only vegetables for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 高之理雪，故懍菜食，鄉里稱之。

translations.literal: Gaozhi's case was cleared, so Lin ate only vegetables, and the neighborhood praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozhi's case was cleared, Lin kept to a vegetarian diet, and people in the neighborhood praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 在元帝府，府中多言其矯。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yuan's princely residence, many in the household said he was putting on an act.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Emperor Yuan's princely household, many there said he was only pretending.

sentences.zh: 至是，大進魚肉，國子祭酒沛國劉玨讓之曰：「本知卿不忠，猶謂卿孝。

translations.literal: At this time he greatly increased fish and meat in his diet. Liu Jue, Director of the Imperial Academy from Pei, reproached him, saying: "I already knew you were not loyal; I still thought you were filial. Today you have neither loyalty nor filial piety.
