translations.idiomatic: Then he greatly increased the fish and meat in his diet. Liu Jue, Director of the Imperial Academy from Pei, rebuked him: "I already knew you were not loyal, but I still thought you filial. Today you have proved yourself devoid of both.

sentences.zh: 今日便是忠孝並無。」

translations.literal: Today you are devoid of both loyalty and filial piety".
translations.idiomatic: Today you are devoid of both loyalty and filial piety".

sentences.zh: 懍不能對。

translations.literal: Lin could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had no answer.

sentences.zh: 懍博學有才藻，口未嘗譽人，朋友以此少之。

translations.literal: Lin was broadly learned and talented in composition, yet never praised anyone in speech, and for this his friends thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was broadly learned and gifted in letters, yet he never praised anyone in speech, and his friends thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 初，侯景平後，梁元帝議還建鄴，唯懍勸都渚宮，以鄉在荊州故也。

translations.literal: At first, after Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan of Liang deliberated on returning to Jiankang; only Lin urged making Zhugong the capital, because his home district lay in Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was suppressed, Emperor Yuan of Liang debated returning the capital to Jiankang; Lin alone urged keeping the court at Zhugong, because his home lay in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 及江陵平，與王褒等入關。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he entered the pass together with Wang Bao and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, he entered the pass together with Wang Bao and others.

sentences.zh: 周文帝以懍名重南土，甚禮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou, because Lin's name was weighty in the south, treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou, knowing Lin's reputation in the south, treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Lin was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with the third rank of ceremonial parity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Lin was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with the third rank of ceremonial parity.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，又與王褒等在麟趾刊定群書，數蒙宴賜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he again joined Wang Bao and others at Linzhi in collating the books of the realm and repeatedly received banquet gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he again joined Wang Bao and others at Linzhi in collating the books of the realm and was repeatedly honored at banquets.

sentences.zh: 保定中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Baoding era.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty scrolls circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of his writings in twenty scrolls circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 劉璠，字寶義，沛人也。

translations.literal: Liu Fan, style name Baoyi, was a native of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan, whose style name was Baoyi, came from Pei.

sentences.zh: 六世祖敏，以永嘉亂，徙居廣陵。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Min, because of the Yongjia chaos, moved to settle in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Min, fleeing the chaos of the Yongjia era, moved the family to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 父臧，性方正，篤志好學，居家以孝聞。

translations.literal: His father Zang was upright in character, devoted in will and fond of learning, and at home was known for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zang was upright in character, devoted to learning, and renowned at home for filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，為著作郎。

translations.literal: He served Liang as a Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as a Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 璠九歲而孤，居喪合禮。

translations.literal: Fan at nine years lost his father and observed mourning in accordance with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Fan lost his father at nine and observed mourning in full accordance with ritual.

sentences.zh: 少好讀書，兼善文筆。

translations.literal: In youth he loved reading and was also skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved books and was also skilled with the brush.

sentences.zh: 十七，為上黃侯蕭曄所器重。

translations.literal: At seventeen he was deeply valued by the Marquis of Shanghuang, Xiao Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he won the deep esteem of the Marquis of Shanghuang, Xiao Ye.

sentences.zh: 范陽張綰，梁之外戚，才高口辯，見推於世。

translations.literal: Zhang Wan of Fanyang, an in-law of Liang, was talented and eloquent and was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wan of Fanyang, a Liang imperial in-law, was talented and eloquent and widely admired.

sentences.zh: 以曄懿貴，亦假借之。

translations.literal: Because Ye was honored and noble, Wan also leaned on him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ye was of high rank and noble birth, Wan also relied on his patronage.

sentences.zh: 璠年少未仕，而負才使氣，不為之屈。

translations.literal: Fan was young and had not yet taken office, yet relied on his talent and was proud in spirit, and would not yield to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was still young and had not yet entered office, yet trusting in his talent and proud in spirit, he would not defer to Wan.

sentences.zh: 綰嘗于新渝侯宅，因酒後詬京兆杜杲曰：「寒士不遜。」

translations.literal: Once at the residence of the Marquis of Xinyu, Wan, after wine, reviled Du Gao of Jingzhao, saying: "A poor scholar shows no deference".
translations.idiomatic: Once at the residence of the Marquis of Xinyu, Wan, after drinking, reviled Du Gao of Jingzhao: "A poor scholar knows no deference".

sentences.zh: 璠厲色曰：「此坐誰非寒士？」

translations.literal: Fan said sternly: "Who at this gathering is not a poor scholar?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan said sharply, "Who at this table is not a poor scholar?"

sentences.zh: 璠本意在綰，而曄以為屬己，辭色不平。

translations.literal: Fan's words were really aimed at Wan, but Ye thought they were directed at himself and showed displeasure in face and speech.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's remark was really aimed at Wan, but Ye thought it was meant for him and showed his displeasure.

sentences.zh: 璠曰：「何王之門不可曳長裾也！」

translations.literal: Fan said: "Under whose gate may one not trail a long robe"!
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, "Under whose gate may one not trail a long robe"!

sentences.zh: 遂拂衣而去。

translations.literal: Then he shook out his robes and left.
translations.idiomatic: With that he shook out his robes and walked away.

sentences.zh: 曄謝之，乃止。

translations.literal: Ye apologized, and only then did Fan stop.
translations.idiomatic: Ye apologized, and only then did Fan relent.

sentences.zh: 後隨曄在淮南。

translations.literal: Later he followed Ye to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Ye to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 璠母在建康遘疾，璠弗之知。

translations.literal: Fan's mother fell ill in Jiankang, and Fan did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's mother fell ill in Jiankang, but Fan knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 嘗忽一日舉身楚痛，尋而家信至，雲其母病。

translations.literal: Suddenly one day his whole body was racked with pain; soon a letter from home arrived saying his mother was ill.
translations.idiomatic: One day his whole body was suddenly racked with pain; soon afterward a letter from home arrived saying his mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 璠即號泣戒道，絕而又蘇。

translations.literal: Fan at once wailed and prepared to travel; he stopped breathing and revived.
translations.idiomatic: Fan at once wailed and set out on the road; he stopped breathing and revived.

sentences.zh: 當身痛之辰，即母死之日。

translations.literal: The day his body was in pain was exactly the day his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: The day his body was racked with pain was exactly the day his mother died.

sentences.zh: 居喪毀瘠，遂感風氣，服闋後一年，猶杖而後起。

translations.literal: In mourning he wasted away; he then contracted wind illness, and a full year after the mourning period ended he still needed a staff before he could rise.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he wasted away and then contracted a wind ailment; even a year after the mourning period ended he still needed a staff to rise.

sentences.zh: 及曄終於毗陵，故吏多分散，璠獨奉曄喪還都，墳成乃退。

translations.literal: When Ye died at Piling, many former subordinates scattered, but Fan alone escorted Ye's coffin back to the capital and withdrew only after the tomb was completed.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye died at Piling, many of his former subordinates scattered, but Fan alone escorted the coffin back to the capital and withdrew only after the tomb was finished.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文暼寺在東宮，遇曄素重，諸不送者多被劾責，唯璠獨被優嘗賞。

translations.literal: When Jianwen of Liang was at the Eastern Palace, since Ye had long been held in esteem, many who did not attend the funeral were impeached and punished, but Fan alone received special commendation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen of Liang was crown prince at the Eastern Palace, Ye had long been held in high esteem, and many who failed to attend his funeral were impeached and punished; Fan alone received special commendation and reward.

sentences.zh: 解褐王國常侍，非其好也。

translations.literal: On first appointment he became Regular Attendant of the princely domain, which was not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: On first taking office he became Regular Attendant of a princely domain, a post that did not suit him.

sentences.zh: 璠少慷慨，好功名，志欲立事邊城，不樂隨牒平進。

translations.literal: Fan from youth was generous and fond of fame and merit, resolved to achieve deeds on the frontier, and did not delight in advancing step by step through routine appointments.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Fan was generous and hungered for fame and achievement; he wished to make his mark on the frontier and took no pleasure in routine promotion.

sentences.zh: 曾宜豐侯蕭脩出為北徐州刺史，即請為其輕車府主簿，兼記室參軍。

translations.literal: Once when the Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xiu, went out as Governor of Northern Xu Province, Fan at once asked to serve as Master of Records in his Light Chariot Office and concurrently as Recording Army Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xiu, was appointed Governor of Northern Xu Province, Fan at once asked to serve as Master of Records in his Light Chariot Office and concurrently as Recording Army Adjutant.

sentences.zh: 脩為梁州，又板為中記室，補華陽太守。

translations.literal: When Xiu was made Governor of Liang Province, Fan was again appointed by written commission as Senior Master of Records and supplemented as Administrator of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu became Governor of Liang Province, Fan was again appointed by written commission as Senior Master of Records and made Administrator of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 屬侯景度江，梁室大亂，脩以璠有才略，甚親委之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and the Liang court fell into great disorder, Xiu, because Fan had talent and strategy, entrusted him with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and the Liang court fell into chaos, Xiu, recognizing Fan's talent and strategic mind, entrusted him with great confidence.

sentences.zh: 時寇難繁興，未有所定，璠乃喟然賦詩以見志。

translations.literal: At that time raids and troubles arose in profusion and nothing was settled; Fan sighed and composed a poem to express his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Raids and troubles arose on every side and nothing was settled; Fan sighed and composed a poem to declare his resolve.

sentences.zh: 其末章曰：「隨會平王室，夷吾匡霸功。

translations.literal: Its final stanza says: "Sui Hui stabilized the royal house; Guan Zhong restored hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Its final stanza reads: "Sui Hui stabilized the royal house; Guan Zhong restored hegemony.

sentences.zh: 虛薄而時用，徒然慕昔風。」

translations.literal: I am slight in talent yet used by the times; in vain I admire the winds of old".
translations.idiomatic: I am slight in talent yet used by the times; in vain I admire the heroes of old".

sentences.zh: 脩開府，置佐史，以璠為諮議參軍，仍領記室。

translations.literal: When Xiu opened a princely headquarters and established aides and clerks, he made Fan Consulting Army Adjutant and still head of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu opened a princely headquarters and appointed aides and clerks, he made Fan Consulting Army Adjutant and still head of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制，授樹功將軍、鎮西府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed provisional authority, Fan was appointed General Who Establishes Merit and Consulting Army Adjutant of the Pacifying West Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed provisional authority, Fan was appointed General Who Establishes Merit and Consulting Army Adjutant of the Pacifying West Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 賜書曰：「鄧禹文學，尚或執戈；

translations.literal: An imperial letter said: "Deng Yu was a man of letters, yet still took up arms;
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter said, "Deng Yu was a man of letters, yet still took up arms;

sentences.zh: 葛洪書生，且雲破賊。

translations.literal: Ge Hong was a scholar, and yet it is said he broke bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong was a scholar, and yet it is said he broke bandits.

sentences.zh: 前修無遠，屬望良深。」

translations.literal: The ancients are not far off; my hopes for you are deep indeed".
translations.idiomatic: The ancients are not far off; my hopes for you run very deep".

sentences.zh: 元帝尋以脩紹鄱陽之封，且為雍州刺史，復以璠為為脩平北府司馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan soon had Xiu succeed to the fief of Poyang and also made him Governor of Yong Province, and again appointed Fan as Chief of Staff of Xiu's Pacifying North Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan soon had Xiu succeed to the fief of Poyang and also made him Governor of Yong Province, and again appointed Fan Chief of Staff of Xiu's Pacifying North Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及武陵王紀稱制於蜀，以璠為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, declared himself emperor in Shu, he made Fan Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, declared himself emperor in Shu, he made Fan Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遣召璠，使者八反，乃至蜀。

translations.literal: He sent to summon Fan; the envoy came back eight times before Fan finally reached Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent to summon Fan; the envoy returned eight times before Fan finally reached Shu.

sentences.zh: 又以為黃門侍郎，令長史劉孝勝深布心腹，使工畫《陳平度河歸漢圖》以遺之。

translations.literal: He again made Fan Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and ordered Chief Clerk Liu Xiaosheng to plant trusted men deeply and had an artist paint "Chen Ping Crossing the River to Return to Han" as a gift to him.
translations.idiomatic: He again made Fan Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and ordered Chief Clerk Liu Xiaosheng to plant trusted agents deeply; he also had an artist paint "Chen Ping Crossing the River to Return to Han" and sent it to Fan as a gift.

sentences.zh: 璠苦求還，中記室韋登私曰：「殿下忍而蓄憾，足下不留，將致大禍。

translations.literal: Fan bitterly begged to return. Senior Master of Records Wei Deng said privately: "The Prince broods and harbors resentment; if you do not stay, great disaster will come. If bandits waylay you at Jiameng, you will be finished. Would it not be better to build the great house together and let body and name both shine?
translations.idiomatic: Fan bitterly begged to return. Senior Master of Records Wei Deng said privately, "The Prince broods and harbors resentment; if you do not stay, great disaster will follow. If robbers waylay you at Jiameng, you are finished. Would it not be better to build the great house together and let your person and your name both shine?

sentences.zh: 脫使盜遮於葭萌，則卿殆矣。

translations.literal: If bandits waylay you at Jiameng, you will be finished.
translations.idiomatic: If robbers waylay you at Jiameng, you are finished.

sentences.zh: 孰若共構大廈，使身名俱美哉！」

translations.literal: Would it not be better to build the great house together and let body and name both shine"?
translations.idiomatic: Would it not be better to build the great house together and let your person and your name both shine"?

sentences.zh: 璠正色曰：「卿欲緩頰於我邪？

translations.literal: Fan said sternly: "Do you wish to soften my resolve?
translations.idiomatic: Fan said sternly, "Do you wish to soften my resolve?

sentences.zh: 我與府侯分義已定，豈以寵辱夷險易其心乎！

translations.literal: My bond with the Prince is already fixed in duty; how could favor and disgrace, ease and danger, change my heart?
translations.idiomatic: My bond with the Prince is already fixed in duty; how could favor and disgrace, ease and danger, change my heart?

sentences.zh: 丈夫立志，當死生以之耳。

translations.literal: A man who sets his will should hold to it through life and death.
translations.idiomatic: A man who sets his will should hold to it through life and death.

sentences.zh: 殿下方布大義於天下，終不逞志於一人。」

translations.literal: Your Highness is now spreading great righteousness throughout the realm; in the end he will not indulge his whim against one man."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is now spreading great righteousness throughout the realm; in the end he will not indulge his whim against one man."

sentences.zh: 紀知不為己用，乃厚贈而遣之。

translations.literal: Ji knew Fan would not serve his purposes, so he gave him rich gifts and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Ji knew Fan would not serve his purposes, so he gave him rich gifts and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 臨別，紀又解其佩刀贈璠曰：「想見物思人。」

translations.literal: At parting Ji again unfastened his girdle knife and gave it to Fan, saying: "When you see this object, think of the man".
translations.idiomatic: At parting Ji again unfastened his girdle knife and gave it to Fan, saying, "When you see this object, think of the man".

sentences.zh: 璠曰：「敢不奉揚威靈，克翦奸宄。」

translations.literal: Fan said: "How dare I fail to carry forth your authority and cut down traitors and rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, "How dare I fail to carry forth your authority and cut down traitors and rebels?"

sentences.zh: 紀於是遣使拜脩為益州刺史，封隨郡王，以璠為府長史，加蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: Ji thereupon sent an envoy to appoint Xiu Governor of Yi Province, enfeoff him as Prince of Suichun, and make Fan Chief of Staff and concurrently Administrator of Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ji thereupon sent an envoy to appoint Xiu Governor of Yi Province, enfeoff him as Prince of Suichun, and make Fan Chief of Staff and concurrently Administrator of Shu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 還至白馬西，屬達奚武軍已至南鄭，璠不得入城，遂降武。

translations.literal: On returning west to White Horse, Daxi Wu's army had already reached Nanzheng, and Fan could not enter the city, so he surrendered to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On returning west to White Horse, Daxi Wu's army had already reached Nanzheng; Fan could not enter the city and surrendered to Wu.

sentences.zh: 周文帝素聞其名，先戒武曰：「勿使劉璠死。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou had long heard Fan's name and beforehand warned Wu, saying: "Do not let Liu Fan die".
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou had long heard Fan's name and beforehand warned Wu: "Do not let Liu Fan die".

sentences.zh: 故武先令璠赴闕。

translations.literal: Therefore Wu first had Fan go to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Wu first sent Fan to the capital.

sentences.zh: 周文見之如舊，謂僕射申徽曰：「劉璠佳士，古人何以過之！」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen received him as of old and said to Vice Director Shen Hui: "Liu Fan is an excellent man—how did the ancients surpass him"!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen received him as of old and said to Vice Director Shen Hui, "Liu Fan is an excellent man—how did the ancients surpass him"!

sentences.zh: 徽曰：「晉人滅吳，利在二陸。

translations.literal: Hui said: "When the Jin people destroyed Wu, the profit lay in the two Lus.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "When the Jin destroyed Wu, the profit lay in the two Lus.

sentences.zh: 明公今平梁漢，得劉璠也。」

translations.literal: Your lordship now pacifies Liang and Han and has gained Liu Fan."
translations.idiomatic: Your lordship now pacifies Liang and Han and has gained Liu Fan."

sentences.zh: 時南鄭尚拒守，達奚武請屠之，周文將許焉，唯令全脩一家而已。

translations.literal: At that time Nanzheng still held out in defense. Daxi Wu requested to slaughter the city; Emperor Wen was about to consent, ordering only that Xiu's household be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzheng still held out in defense. Daxi Wu asked to slaughter the city; Emperor Wen was about to consent, ordering only that Xiu's household be spared.

sentences.zh: 璠乃請之于朝，周文怒而不許也。

translations.literal: Fan then pleaded at court; Emperor Wen was angry and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Fan then pleaded at court, but Emperor Wen was angry and refused.

sentences.zh: 璠泣而固請，移時不退。

translations.literal: Fan wept and firmly pleaded, and for a long time would not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Fan wept and pleaded firmly, and for a long time would not withdraw.

sentences.zh: 柳仲禮侍側，曰：「此烈士也。」

translations.literal: Liu Zhongli, attending at his side, said: "This is a man of heroic resolve".
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongli, attending at his side, said, "This is a man of heroic resolve".

sentences.zh: 周文既納蕭脩降，又許其反國。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen both accepted Xiao Xiu's surrender and promised that he might return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen both accepted Xiao Xiu's surrender and promised that he might return to his state.

sentences.zh: 脩至長安累月，未之遣也。

translations.literal: Xiu reached Chang'an and for months was not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu reached Chang'an and for months was not sent back.

sentences.zh: 璠因侍宴，周文曰：「我于古誰比？」

translations.literal: Fan, while attending a banquet, was asked by Emperor Wen: "Among the ancients, to whom do you compare me"?
translations.idiomatic: While attending a banquet, Fan was asked by Emperor Wen, "Among the ancients, to whom do you compare me"?

sentences.zh: 曰：「常以公命世英主，湯、武莫逮。

translations.literal: He said: "I have always regarded Your Lordship as a hero of the age; even Tang and Wu could not match you.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I have always regarded Your Lordship as a hero of the age; even Tang and Wu could not match you.

sentences.zh: 今日所見，曾是齊桓、晉文之不若。」

translations.literal: What I see today falls short even of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin."
translations.idiomatic: What I see today falls short even of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin."

sentences.zh: 周文曰：「我不得比湯、武，望與伊、周為匹，何桓、文之不若乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said: "I cannot compare with Tang and Wu; I hope to be the equal of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—why fall short of Huan and Wen?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said, "I cannot compare with Tang and Wu; I hope to stand equal to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—why should I fall short of Huan and Wen?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「齊桓存三亡國，晉文不失信于伐原。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Duke Huan of Qi preserved three extinguished states; Duke Wen of Jin did not break faith in the campaign against Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Duke Huan of Qi preserved three extinguished states; Duke Wen of Jin did not break faith in the campaign against Yuan."

sentences.zh: 語未終，周文撫掌曰：「我解爾意，欲激我耳。」

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking, Emperor Wen clapped his hands and said: "I understand your meaning—you wish to spur me on."
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished speaking, Emperor Wen clapped his hands and said, "I understand your meaning—you wish to spur me on."

sentences.zh: 即命遣脩。

translations.literal: He at once ordered Xiu sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He at once ordered Xiu sent back.

sentences.zh: 脩請與璠俱還，周文不許。

translations.literal: Xiu asked to return together with Fan; Emperor Wen would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu asked to return together with Fan, but Emperor Wen refused.

sentences.zh: 以璠為中外府記室，遷黃門侍郎、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Fan was made Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters, then promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate with the third rank of ceremonial parity.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was made Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters, then promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate with the third rank of ceremonial parity.

sentences.zh: 嘗臥疾居家，對雪興感，乃作《雪賦》以遂志焉。

translations.literal: Once, ill at home, he was moved by the sight of snow and composed the "Rhapsody on Snow" to express his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Once, ill at home, he was moved by the sight of snow and composed the "Rhapsody on Snow" to express his resolve.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭脩在漢中與蕭紀箋，及答西魏書、移襄陽文，皆璠辭也。

translations.literal: At first, when Xiao Xiu was in Hanzhong, his letters to Xiao Ji and his replies to Western Wei's letters and his proclamation to Xiangyang were all Fan's compositions.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xiu was in Hanzhong, his letters to Xiao Ji, his replies to Western Wei, and his proclamation to Xiangyang were all written by Fan.

sentences.zh: 周明帝初，授內史中大夫，掌綸誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Zhou's reign, Fan was appointed Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat and put in charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Zhou's reign, Fan was appointed Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat and put in charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 尋封平陽縣子。

translations.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 在職清白簡亮，不合于時。

translations.literal: In office he was pure, white, concise, and bright, and did not fit the times.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was pure, upright, and plainspoken, and did not fit the temper of the times.

sentences.zh: 左遷同和郡守。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Administrator of Tonghe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Administrator of Tonghe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 璠善於撫禦，蒞職未期，生羌降附者五百餘家。

translations.literal: Fan was skilled in comforting and controlling; within one term of office more than five hundred households of raw Qiang submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was skilled at winning people over; within a single term more than five hundred households of raw Qiang submitted.

sentences.zh: 前後郡守多經營以致貲產，唯璠秋毫無所取。

translations.literal: Former and later commandery administrators mostly engaged in business to amass property; Fan alone took not the slightest thing.
translations.idiomatic: Former and later commandery administrators mostly engaged in business to amass property; Fan alone took not the slightest thing.

sentences.zh: 妻子並隨羌俗，食麥衣皮，始終不改。

translations.literal: Wife and children all followed Qiang custom, eating wheat and wearing skins, and from beginning to end did not change.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children all followed Qiang custom, eating wheat and wearing skins, and never changed their ways.

sentences.zh: 洮陽、洪和二郡羌常越境詣璠番訟理。

translations.literal: The Qiang of Taoyang and Honghe commanderies often crossed the border to bring lawsuits before Fan for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang of Taoyang and Honghe commanderies often crossed the border to bring lawsuits before Fan for judgment.

sentences.zh: 蔡公廣時鎮隴右，嘉其善政。

translations.literal: Duke Cai Guang at that time was stationed in Longyou and praised his good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Cai Guang, then stationed in Longyou, praised his good governance.

sentences.zh: 及遷鎮陝州，欲啟璠自隨，羌人樂從者七百人，聞者莫不歎異。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to station at Shaan Province, he wished to have Fan accompany him; seven hundred Qiang gladly followed, and all who heard of it sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to station at Shaan Province, he wished to have Fan accompany him; seven hundred Qiang gladly followed, and all who heard of it marveled.

sentences.zh: 陳公純作鎮隴右，引為總管府司錄，甚禮敬之。

translations.literal: Duke Chen Chun, when stationed in Longyou, summoned Fan as Chief Clerk of the Regional Headquarters and treated him with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Chen Chun was stationed in Longyou, he summoned Fan as Chief Clerk of the Regional Headquarters and treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 著梁典三十卷，有集二十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote the Liang Canon in thirty scrolls and had a collected works in twenty scrolls circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Liang Canon in thirty scrolls and left a collected works in twenty scrolls that circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 子祥。

translations.literal: His son was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 祥字休徵。

translations.literal: Xiang, style name Xiuzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, whose style name was Xiuzheng.

sentences.zh: 幼聰慧，賓客見者皆號神童。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and intelligent; all guests who saw him called him a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; every guest who saw him called him a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 事嫡母以至孝聞。

translations.literal: In serving his stepmother he was known for utmost filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his stepmother he was known for utmost filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 其伯父黃門郎璆，有名江左，在嶺南，聞而奇之，乃令名祥字休徵。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Qiu, was famous east of the Yangtze; hearing of him in Lingnan, he marveled and therefore had him named Xiang with the style Xiuzheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Qiu, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, was famous east of the Yangtze; hearing of the boy in Lingnan, he marveled and had him named Xiang with the style Xiuzheng.

sentences.zh: 後以字行於世。

translations.literal: Later he was known in the world by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was known in the world by his style name.

sentences.zh: 十歲能屬文，十二通《五經》。

translations.literal: At ten he could compose prose; at twelve he mastered the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could compose prose; at twelve he had mastered the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，為宜豐侯記室參軍。

translations.literal: He served Liang as Recording Army Adjutant to the Marquis of Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as Recording Army Adjutant to the Marquis of Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，隨例入關中。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he entered the pass according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, he entered the pass with the other captives.

sentences.zh: 齊公憲召為記室，府中書記皆令掌之。

translations.literal: Duke Yuwen Xian summoned him as Master of Records, and all documents in the princely headquarters were put under his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yuwen Xian summoned him as Master of Records, and all documents in the princely headquarters were put under his charge.

sentences.zh: 封漢安縣子。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Han'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Han'an.

sentences.zh: 憲進爵為王，以休徵為王友。

translations.literal: When Xian advanced in rank to prince, Xiuzheng was made Friend of the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was raised to princely rank, Xiuzheng was made Friend of the Prince.

sentences.zh: 俄除內史上士。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Senior Clerk of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Senior Clerk of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝東征，休徵陪侍帷幄，平齊露布即休徵文也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned east, Xiuzheng attended him in the command tent; the victory bulletin on the pacification of Qi was Xiuzheng's composition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu campaigned east, Xiuzheng attended him in the command tent; the victory bulletin on the pacification of Qi was written by Xiuzheng.

sentences.zh: 累遷車騎大將軍、儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand General with the great rank of ceremonial parity.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand General with the great rank of ceremonial parity.

sentences.zh: 曆長安、萬年二縣令，頗獲時譽。

translations.literal: He successively served as Magistrate of Chang'an and Wannian counties and won considerable praise in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as magistrate of Chang'an and Wannian counties and won considerable praise in his time.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 初，璠所選《梁典》始就，未及刊定而卒，臨終謂休徵曰：「能成我志，其在此書乎！」

translations.literal: At first the Liang Canon that Fan compiled was just finished but had not yet been edited and published when he died; on his deathbed he told Xiuzheng: "To fulfill my wish—will it not lie in this book"!
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Canon that Fan had compiled was just finished but not yet edited and published when he died; on his deathbed he told Xiuzheng, "To fulfill my wish—will it not lie in this book"!

sentences.zh: 休徵修定繕寫。

translations.literal: Xiuzheng edited, corrected, and copied it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzheng edited, corrected, and copied it.

sentences.zh: 勒成一家，行於世。

translations.literal: He completed it as a work in its own right, and it circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He brought it to completion as a work in its own right, and it circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 行本，璠兄子也。

translations.literal: Xingben was Fan's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xingben was the son of Fan's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 父環，仕梁，曆職清顯。

translations.literal: His father Huan served Liang and successively held clear, eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huan served Liang and successively held clear, eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 行本起家梁武陵王國常侍。

translations.literal: Xingben first took office as Regular Attendant of the Princely Domain of Wuling of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xingben first entered office as Regular Attendant of the Princely Domain of Wuling of Liang.

sentences.zh: 遇蕭脩以梁州北附，遂與叔父璠歸周，寓居新豐。

translations.literal: When Xiao Xiu brought Liang Province north to submit, he then returned to Zhou together with his uncle Fan and lodged in Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xiu brought Liang Province north to submit, he returned to Zhou together with his uncle Fan and made his home in Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 每以諷讀為事，精力忘疲，雖衣食乏絕，晏如也。

translations.literal: He always made recitation and reading his occupation, forgetting fatigue in his energy; though food and clothing were exhausted, he was perfectly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He always made recitation and reading his occupation, driving himself without fatigue; though food and clothing ran short, he remained perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 性剛烈，有不可奪之志。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and resolute, with a will that could not be wrested away.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stern and resolute, with a will that could not be wrested away.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為中外府記室。

translations.literal: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of Zhou, summoned him as Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of Zhou, summoned him as Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 武帝親總萬機，轉禦正中士，兼領起居注。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Xingben was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently put in charge of the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Xingben was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently put in charge of the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 累遷掌朝下大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Court Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Court Attendance.

sentences.zh: 周代故事，天子臨軒，掌朝典筆硯，持至御坐，則承禦大夫取進之。

translations.literal: By Zhou custom, when the Son of Heaven faced the hall, the Court Attendance Master held the brush and inkstone and, when he reached the imperial seat, the Assistant Master of Attendance took them and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhou custom, when the Son of Heaven faced the hall, the Court Attendance Master held the brush and inkstone and, on reaching the imperial seat, the Assistant Master of Attendance took them and presented them.

sentences.zh: 及行本為掌朝，將進筆於帝，承禦復欲取之。

translations.literal: When Xingben was Court Attendance Master and was about to present the brush to the Emperor, the Assistant Master again wished to take it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingben was Court Attendance Master and was about to present the brush to the Emperor, the Assistant Master again tried to take it.

sentences.zh: 行本抗聲曰：「筆不可得。」

translations.literal: Xingben said loudly: "The brush cannot be taken".
translations.idiomatic: Xingben said loudly, "The brush cannot be taken".

sentences.zh: 帝驚視問之，行本曰：「臣聞設官分職，各有司存。

translations.literal: The Emperor looked up in surprise and asked why; Xingben said: "I have heard that in establishing offices one divides duties, and each has its keeper.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor looked up in surprise and asked why; Xingben said, "I have heard that in establishing offices one divides duties, and each has its keeper.

sentences.zh: 臣既不得佩承禦刀，承禦亦焉得取臣筆？」

translations.literal: Since I may not wear the Assistant Master's knife at my belt, how may the Assistant Master take my brush?"
translations.idiomatic: Since I may not wear the Assistant Master's knife at my belt, how may the Assistant Master take my brush?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "So it is."

sentences.zh: 因令二司各行所職。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered the two offices each to perform its own duty.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered the two offices each to perform its own duty.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝嗣位，多失德，行本切諫忤旨，出為河內太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne and often lost virtue, Xingben remonstrated sharply and offended the imperial will; he was sent out as Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne and often lost virtue, Xingben remonstrated sharply and offended the imperial will; he was sent out as Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥作亂，攻懷州，行本率吏人拒之，拜儀同，賜爵文安縣子。

translations.literal: When Wei Chijiong rebelled and attacked Huaizhou, Xingben led clerks and people to resist him; he was appointed with ceremonial parity and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Chijiong rebelled and attacked Huaizhou, Xingben led clerks and people to resist him; he was granted ceremonial parity and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐祚，拜諫議大夫，檢校中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, Xingben was appointed Remonstrance Grand Master and Inspector of Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, Xingben was appointed Remonstrance Grand Master and Inspector of Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上嘗怒一郎，於殿前笞之。

translations.literal: Once the Emperor was angry with a Gentleman and had him beaten with the rod before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Emperor was angry with a Gentleman and had him beaten with the rod before the hall.

sentences.zh: 行本進曰：「此人素清，其過又小。」

translations.literal: Xingben stepped forward and said: "This man has always been upright, and his offense is small".
translations.idiomatic: Xingben stepped forward and said, "This man has always been upright, and his offense is small".

sentences.zh: 上不顧。

translations.literal: The Emperor paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 行本正當上前曰：「陛下不以臣不肖，令臣在左右。

translations.literal: Xingben stood directly before the Emperor and said: "Your Majesty, knowing I am unworthy, still keeps me at your side.
translations.idiomatic: Xingben stood directly before the Emperor and said, "Your Majesty, knowing I am unworthy, still keeps me at your side.

sentences.zh: 臣言若是，陛下安得不聽？

translations.literal: If my words are right, how can Your Majesty fail to heed them?
translations.idiomatic: If my words are right, how can Your Majesty fail to heed them?

sentences.zh: 臣言若非，當致之于理，安得輕臣而不顧？

translations.literal: If my words are wrong, I should be handed over to the law; how can Your Majesty lightly disregard me and pay no heed?
translations.idiomatic: If my words are wrong, I should be handed over to the law; how can Your Majesty lightly disregard me and pay no heed?

sentences.zh: 臣所言非私！」

translations.literal: What I say is not for private ends"!
translations.idiomatic: What I say is not for private ends"!

sentences.zh: 因置笏於地而退，上斂容謝之，遂原所笞者。

translations.literal: He then laid down his tablet and withdrew; the Emperor composed his face and apologized, and finally pardoned the man who had been beaten.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid down his tablet and withdrew; the Emperor composed his face and apologized, and finally pardoned the man who had been beaten.

sentences.zh: 時天下大同，四夷內附，行本以党項羌密邇封域，最為後服，上表劾其使者曰：「臣聞南蠻遵校尉之統，西域仰都護之威。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was united and the four barbarians submitted within; Xingben, because the Tangut Qiang lay close to the border and were the last to submit, memorialized impeaching their envoy, saying: "I have heard that the southern barbarians obey the command of the Commandant, and the Western Regions look to the Protector-General's authority.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm was united and the four barbarians submitted within; Xingben, because the Tangut Qiang lay close to the border and were the last to submit, memorialized impeaching their envoy: "I have heard that the southern barbarians obey the command of the Commandant, and the Western Regions look to the Protector-General's authority.

sentences.zh: 比見西羌，鼠竊狗盜，不父不子，無君無臣，異類殊方，於斯為下。

translations.literal: Of late I have seen the western Qiang, thieving like rats and dogs, neither fathering nor sonning, without lord or minister—a foreign race in a distant land, lowest of all.
translations.idiomatic: Of late I have seen the western Qiang, thieving like rats and dogs, neither honoring fathers nor rearing sons, without lord or minister—a foreign race in a distant land, lowest of all.

sentences.zh: 不悟羈縻之惠，詎知含養之恩，狼戾為心，獨乖正朔。

translations.literal: They do not understand the grace of bridled submission, nor know the kindness of nurturing care; wolfish and unruly in heart, they alone defy the royal calendar.
translations.idiomatic: They do not understand the grace of bridled submission, nor know the kindness of nurturing care; wolfish and unruly in heart, they alone defy the royal calendar.

sentences.zh: 使人近至，請付推科。」

translations.literal: Their envoy has just arrived; I ask that he be handed over for investigation and punishment".
translations.idiomatic: Their envoy has just arrived; I ask that he be handed over for investigation and punishment".

sentences.zh: 上奇其志。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor marveled at his resolve.

sentences.zh: 雍州別駕元肇言於上曰：「有一州吏，受人饋錢二百文，律令杖一百。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhao, Assistant Administrator of Yong Province, said to the Emperor: "There was a clerk of one province who received two hundred cash in gifts; by law he should be beaten one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhao, Assistant Administrator of Yong Province, said to the Emperor, "There was a clerk of one province who received two hundred cash in gifts; by law he should be beaten one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 然臣下車之始，與其為約。

translations.literal: Yet when I first took office I made an agreement with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when I first took office I made an agreement with him.

sentences.zh: 此吏故違，請加徒一年。」

translations.literal: This clerk deliberately violated it; I ask that one year of penal servitude be added".
translations.idiomatic: This clerk deliberately violated it; I ask that one year of penal servitude be added".

sentences.zh: 行本駁之曰：「律令之行，蓋發明詔。

translations.literal: Xingben rebutted him, saying: "The execution of laws and orders should clarify the imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Xingben rebutted him, saying, "The execution of laws and orders should clarify the imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 今肇乃敢重其教命，輕忽憲章，虧法取威，非人臣之禮。」

translations.literal: Now Zhao dares to aggravate his teaching command and lightly disregard the statutes, damaging the law to seize authority—this is not the rite of a minister."
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhao dares to aggravate his own command and lightly disregard the statutes, damaging the law to seize authority—this is not the conduct of a minister."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised this and bestowed one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised this and bestowed one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 拜太子左庶子，領書侍御史如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent while still serving as Attendant Censor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent while still serving as Attendant Censor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 皇太子虛襟敬憚。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince opened his breast to him in respect and fear.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince treated him with open respect and restraint.

sentences.zh: 時唐令則為左庶子，太子昵狎之，每令以弦歌教內人。

translations.literal: At that time Tang Lingze was Left Assistant; the Crown Prince was intimate with him and often had him teach the inner household with string music.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tang Lingze was Left Assistant; the Crown Prince was intimate with him and often had him teach the inner household with string music.

sentences.zh: 行本責之曰：「庶子當匡太子以正道，何嬖昵房帷之間哉！」

translations.literal: Xingben reproached him, saying: "The Assistant should guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way—why dally in fond intimacy within the bedchamber"!
translations.idiomatic: Xingben reproached him, saying, "The Assistant should guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way—why dally in fond intimacy within the bedchamber"!

sentences.zh: 令則甚慚而不能改。

translations.literal: Lingze was greatly ashamed but could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Lingze was deeply ashamed but could not change.

sentences.zh: 時沛國劉臻、平原明克讓、河南陸爽等並以文學為太子所親。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Zhen of Pei, Ming Keyang of Pingyuan, Lu Shuang of Henan, and others were all favored by the Crown Prince for their literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Zhen of Pei, Ming Keyang of Pingyuan, Lu Shuang of Henan, and others were all favored by the Crown Prince for their literary learning.

sentences.zh: 行本怒其不能調護，每謂三人曰：「卿等正解讀書耳。」

translations.literal: Xingben was angry that they could not guide and protect him, and often said to the three: "You gentlemen only know how to read books, that is all".
translations.idiomatic: Xingben was angry that they could not guide and protect the prince, and often said to the three, "You gentlemen only know how to read books, that is all".

sentences.zh: 時左術率長史夏侯福為太子所昵，嘗於閤內與太子戲。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Clerk of the Left Guard Xiahou Fu was favored by the Crown Prince and once played with the Crown Prince inside the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chief Clerk of the Left Guard Xiahou Fu was favored by the Crown Prince and once played with the Crown Prince inside the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 福大笑，聲聞於外。

translations.literal: Fu laughed loudly, and the sound was heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: Fu laughed loudly, and the sound was heard outside.

sentences.zh: 行本時在閤下聞之，待其出，數之曰：「汝何小人，敢為褻慢！」

translations.literal: Xingben was below the pavilion and heard it; when Fu came out he counted his faults, saying: "What sort of petty man dares behave with such disrespect"!
translations.idiomatic: Xingben was below the pavilion and heard it; when Fu came out he rebuked him, saying, "What sort of petty man dares behave with such disrespect"!

sentences.zh: 因付執法者推之。

translations.literal: He then handed him over to the law officers for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He then handed him over to the law officers for investigation.

sentences.zh: 太子為請，乃釋之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince pleaded for him, and only then was he released.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince pleaded for him, and only then was he released.

sentences.zh: 太子嘗得良馬，令福乘而觀之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince once obtained a fine horse and had Fu ride it to show it off.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince once obtained a fine horse and had Fu ride it to show it off.

sentences.zh: 太子甚悅，因欲令行本復乘。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince was greatly pleased and therefore wished to have Xingben ride it again.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince was greatly pleased and therefore wished to have Xingben ride it as well.

sentences.zh: 行本正色曰：「至尊置臣於庶子位，欲輔導殿下以正道，非為殿下作弄臣。」

translations.literal: Xingben said sternly: "Your Majesty placed me in the post of Assistant to the Heir Apparent to guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way, not to be a plaything for the Crown Prince".
translations.idiomatic: Xingben said sternly, "Your Majesty placed me in the post of Assistant to the Heir Apparent to guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way, not to be a plaything for the Crown Prince".

sentences.zh: 太子慚而止。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince was ashamed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince was ashamed and stopped.

sentences.zh: 復以本官領大興令，權貴憚其方正，無敢至其門者。

translations.literal: He again held his original office and concurrently served as Magistrate of Daxing; the powerful and noble feared his uprightness, and none dared come to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He again held his original office and concurrently served as Magistrate of Daxing; the powerful and noble feared his uprightness, and none dared come to his gate.

sentences.zh: 由是請托路絕，吏人懷之。

translations.literal: Because of this the path of private requests was cut off, and clerks and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the path of private requests was cut off, and clerks and commoners cherished him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒於官，上甚傷惜之。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office, and the Emperor deeply mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office, and the Emperor deeply mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 及太子廢，上曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was deposed, the Emperor said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince was deposed, the Emperor said, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 若使劉行本在，勇當不及此乎！」

translations.literal: If Liu Xingben were still alive, would Prince Yong not have come to this"!
translations.idiomatic: If Liu Xingben were still alive, would Prince Yong not have come to this"!

sentences.zh: 行本無子。

translations.literal: Xingben had no son.
translations.idiomatic: Xingben had no son.

sentences.zh: 柳遐，字子升，河東解人，宋太尉元景從孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Xia, style name Zisheng, was a native of Jie in Hedong and a collateral descendant of Song Grand Marshal Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xia, whose style name was Zisheng, came from Jie in Hedong and was a collateral descendant of Song Grand Marshal Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 祖叔珍，義陽內史，事見《南史》。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuzhen was Administrator of Yiyang; his career is recorded in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuzhen was Administrator of Yiyang; his career is recorded in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 父季遠，梁宜都太守。

translations.literal: His father Jiyuan was Administrator of Yidu under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiyuan served as Administrator of Yidu under Liang.

sentences.zh: 遐幼而爽邁，神彩嶷然，髫歲便有成人之量。

translations.literal: Xia from childhood was bright and lofty; his spirit and bearing were towering, and even in infancy he already had the measure of a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Xia was bright and lofty in spirit; even in infancy he already had the measure of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 篤好文學，動合規矩。

translations.literal: He deeply loved literature and learning, and in action always accorded with rule and measure.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply loved literature and learning, and in conduct always accorded with rule and measure.

sentences.zh: 其世父慶遠特器異之，謂曰：「吾昔逮事伯父太尉公，嘗謂吾云：'我昨夢汝登一樓，甚峻麗，吾以坐席與汝。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Qingyuan especially valued and distinguished him, saying to him: "I once served our father's elder brother the Grand Marshal, and he once told me: 'Yesterday I dreamed that you climbed a tower, very high and splendid, and I gave you my seat cushion.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Qingyuan especially valued him and said, "I once served our father's elder brother the Grand Marshal, and he once told me, 'Yesterday I dreamed that you climbed a tower, very high and splendid, and I gave you my seat cushion.

sentences.zh: 汝後名宦必達，恨吾不及見耳。

translations.literal: Your later fame and office will surely reach far; I regret that I shall not live to see it.
translations.idiomatic: Your later fame and office will surely reach far; I regret that I shall not live to see it.

sentences.zh: '吾向聊復晝寢，又夢將昔時坐席還以賜汝，汝之官位當復及吾。

translations.literal: I have just dozed again in the daytime and dreamed that I gave you back the seat cushion of old; your official rank will again reach mine.
translations.idiomatic: I have just dozed again in the daytime and dreamed that I gave you back the seat cushion of old; your official rank will again reach mine.

sentences.zh: 特宜勉勵，以應嘉祥也。」

translations.literal: You should especially exert yourself to answer this auspicious sign.'"
translations.idiomatic: You should especially exert yourself to answer this auspicious sign.'"

sentences.zh: 梁西昌侯藻鎮雍州，遐時年十二，以百姓禮修謁，風儀端肅，進止詳雅。

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Xichang, Xiao Zao, was stationed at Yong Province, Xia at twelve years of age paid a visit in the manner of a common subject; his bearing was dignified and his movements refined and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Xichang, Xiao Zao, was stationed at Yong Province, Xia at twelve paid a visit in the manner of a common subject; his bearing was dignified and his movements refined and elegant.

sentences.zh: 藻羨之，試遣左右踐遐衣裾，欲觀其舉措。

translations.literal: Zao admired him and tested him by sending attendants to tread on the hem of Xia's robe, wishing to observe his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zao admired him and tested him by sending attendants to tread on the hem of Xia's robe, wishing to observe his conduct.

sentences.zh: 遐徐步稍前，曾不顧盼。

translations.literal: Xia walked slowly forward and never looked back.
translations.idiomatic: Xia walked slowly forward and never looked back.

sentences.zh: 仕梁稍遷尚書功論郎。

translations.literal: Serving Liang, he was gradually promoted to Gentleman of Merit Evaluation in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he was gradually promoted to Gentleman of Merit Evaluation in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 陳郡謝舉時為僕射，引遐與語，甚嘉之，顧謂人曰：「江漢英靈見於此矣。」

translations.literal: Xie Ju of Chen Commandery was then Vice Director; he drew Xia into conversation, greatly praised him, and turning to others said: "The heroic spirit of the Jiang and Han is seen here."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ju of Chen Commandery was then Vice Director; he drew Xia into conversation, greatly praised him, and turning to others said, "The heroic spirit of the Jiang and Han is seen here."

sentences.zh: 岳陽王蕭詧於襄陽承制，授遐吏部郎，賜爵聞喜公。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, assuming provisional authority at Xiangyang, appointed Xia Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed him as Duke of Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, assuming provisional authority at Xiangyang, appointed Xia Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed him as Duke of Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 尋進位持節、侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was further promoted to Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Rapid Cavalry Grand General, and Grand Master with the third rank of ceremonial parity.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was further promoted to Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Rapid Cavalry Grand General, and Grand Master with the third rank of ceremonial parity.

sentences.zh: 及詧踐帝位於江陵，以襄陽來歸，辭詧曰：「陛下中興鼎業，龍飛舊楚。

translations.literal: When Cha ascended the throne at Jiangling and Xiangyang came over in submission, Xia declined Cha, saying: "Your Majesty restores the imperial enterprise in mid-flourish; the dragon flies again in old Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha ascended the throne at Jiangling and Xiangyang came over in submission, Xia declined Cha, saying, "Your Majesty restores the imperial enterprise in mid-flourish; the dragon flies again in old Chu.

sentences.zh: 臣昔因幸會，早奉名節，理當以身許國，期之始終。

translations.literal: I once, through early fortune, early received your honored favor; by right I should devote my body to the state from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: I once, through early fortune, received your honored favor; by right I should devote my body to the state from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 自晉氏南遷臣宗族蓋寡，從祖太尉、世父儀同、從父司空，並以位望隆重，遂家于金陵；

translations.literal: Since the Jin moved south my clan has grown sparse; my collateral ancestor the Grand Marshal, my father's elder brother with ceremonial parity, and my father's younger brother the Minister of Works all, because of weighty rank and eminence, made their home in Jinling;
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin moved south my clan has grown sparse; my collateral ancestor the Grand Marshal, my father's elder brother with ceremonial parity, and my father's younger brother the Minister of Works all, because of weighty rank and eminence, made their home in Jinling;

sentences.zh: 唯留先臣獨守墳栢，嘗誡臣等，使不違此志。

translations.literal: only my late father remained alone to guard the tombs and cypresses, and often admonished us not to violate this resolve.
translations.idiomatic: only my late father remained alone to guard the tombs and cypresses, and often admonished us not to violate this resolve.

sentences.zh: 今襄陽既入北朝，臣若陪隨鑾蹕，進則無益塵露，退則有虧先旨。」

translations.literal: Now that Xiangyang has entered the Northern court, if I follow the imperial carriage, in advancing I would add nothing but dust and dew, and in retreat I would fail my forefathers' intent."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Xiangyang has entered the Northern court, if I followed the imperial carriage, in advancing I would add nothing but dust and dew, and in retreat I would fail my forefathers' intent."

sentences.zh: 詧重違其志，遂許之，因留鄉里，以經籍自娛。

translations.literal: Cha, deeply unwilling to violate his resolve, thereupon consented and left him in his home district to amuse himself with the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Cha, deeply unwilling to violate his resolve, consented and left him in his home district to amuse himself with the classics.

sentences.zh: 周文帝、明帝頻征，固辭以疾。

translations.literal: Emperors Wen and Ming of Zhou repeatedly summoned him, but he firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Wen and Ming of Zhou repeatedly summoned him, but he firmly declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 及詧殂，遐舉哀，行舊臣之服。

translations.literal: When Cha died, Xia observed mourning and wore the garb of an old subject.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha died, Xia observed mourning and wore the garb of an old subject.

sentences.zh: 保定中，又征之，遐始入朝，授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、霍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era he was again summoned; Xia then entered court and was appointed Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Grand Master with the third rank of ceremonial parity, and Governor of Huo Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoding era he was again summoned; Xia then entered court and was appointed Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Grand Master with the third rank of ceremonial parity, and Governor of Huo Province.

sentences.zh: 遐導人務先以德，再三不用命者，乃微加貶異，示恥而已。

translations.literal: Xia in guiding people always put virtue first; only when someone repeatedly disobeyed orders did he lightly impose demotion or distinction, showing shame and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: In guiding people Xia always put virtue first; only when someone repeatedly disobeyed orders did he lightly impose demotion or distinction, showing shame and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 其下感而化之，不復為過，咸曰：「我君仁惠如此，其可欺乎！」

translations.literal: His subordinates were moved and reformed and no longer committed offenses, all saying: "Our lord is so benevolent and gracious—how could we deceive him"!
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates were moved and reformed and no longer committed offenses, all saying, "Our lord is so benevolent and gracious—how could we deceive him"!

sentences.zh: 卒，贈金、安二州刺史。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously appointed Governor of Jin and An provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Governor of Jin and An provinces.

sentences.zh: 遐有至行。

translations.literal: Xia had utmost conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was a man of utmost moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 初為州主簿，其父卒于揚州，遐自襄陽奔赴，六日而至，哀感行路，毀悴不可識。

translations.literal: At first, while Chief Clerk of the province, his father died in Yang Province; Xia rushed from Xiangyang and arrived in six days. Grief moved those on the road, and he was so wasted that he could not be recognized.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Chief Clerk of the province, his father died in Yang Province; Xia rushed from Xiangyang and arrived in six days. Grief moved those on the road, and he was so wasted that he could not be recognized.

sentences.zh: 後奉喪西歸。

translations.literal: Later he escorted the coffin westward.
translations.idiomatic: Later he escorted the coffin westward.

sentences.zh: 中流風起，舟中人相顧失色。

translations.literal: Midstream a wind arose, and those in the boat looked at one another in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Midstream a wind arose, and those in the boat looked at one another in alarm.

sentences.zh: 遐抱棺號慟，訴天求哀，俄頃風止浪息。

translations.literal: Xia embraced the coffin and wailed, crying out to Heaven and begging for pity; in a moment the wind stopped and the waves subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Xia embraced the coffin and wailed, crying out to Heaven and begging for pity; in a moment the wind stopped and the waves subsided.

sentences.zh: 其母嘗乳間發疽，醫云：「此疾無可救理，唯得人吮膿，或望微止其痛。」

translations.literal: His mother once developed a sore between her breasts; the physician said: "This illness cannot be cured; only if someone sucks out the pus may the pain perhaps be slightly eased".
translations.idiomatic: His mother once developed a sore between her breasts; the physician said, "This illness cannot be cured; only if someone sucks out the pus may the pain perhaps be slightly eased".

sentences.zh: 遐應聲即吮，旬日遂瘳。

translations.literal: Xia at once answered and sucked; within ten days she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Xia at once answered and sucked; within ten days she recovered.

sentences.zh: 咸以為孝感所致。

translations.literal: All held that this was caused by filial feeling moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: All held that this was caused by filial devotion moving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 性又溫裕，略無喜慍之容。

translations.literal: By nature he was also warm and generous, with scarcely any look of joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was also warm and generous, with scarcely any look of joy or anger.

sentences.zh: 弘獎名教，未嘗論人之短。

translations.literal: He broadly encouraged the teaching of names and ritual and never discussed people's faults.
translations.idiomatic: He broadly encouraged the teaching of names and ritual and never discussed people's faults.

sentences.zh: 尤尚施與，家無餘財。

translations.literal: He especially valued giving, and his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He especially valued giving, and his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 臨終遺誡簿葬，其子等並奉行之。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he left instructions for a plain burial, and his sons all followed them.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he left instructions for a plain burial, and his sons all followed them.

sentences.zh: 有十子，靖、莊最知名。

translations.literal: He had ten sons; Jing and Zhuang were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons; Jing and Zhuang were the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 靖字思休，少方雅，博覽墳籍。

translations.literal: Jing, style name Sihui, from youth was upright and elegant and broadly read the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, whose style name was Sihui, from youth was upright and elegant and broadly read the classics.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，正員郎。

translations.literal: He served Liang as Regular Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as Regular Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 隨遐入周，授大都督，曆河南、德廣二郡守。

translations.literal: Following Xia into Zhou, he was appointed Grand Commander and successively served as Administrator of Henan and Deguang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Following Xia into Zhou, he was appointed Grand Commander and successively served as Administrator of Henan and Deguang commanderies.

sentences.zh: 所居皆有政術，吏人畏而愛之。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he had governing skill; clerks and people feared yet loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he had governing skill; clerks and commoners feared yet loved him.

sentences.zh: 然性愛閑素，其于名利澹如也。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he loved quiet simplicity, and toward fame and profit he was indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he loved quiet simplicity, and toward fame and profit he was indifferent.

sentences.zh: 及秩滿還鄉，便有終焉之志。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned home and already had the resolve to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned home and already had the resolve to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，特詔征之，以疾固辭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, he was specially summoned by edict, but firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, he was specially summoned by edict but firmly declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 優遊不仕，閉門自守，所對唯琴書如已。

translations.literal: At ease and unoccupied, he kept his door closed and guarded himself; his companions were only the zither and books, as if alone.
translations.idiomatic: At ease and unoccupied, he kept his door closed and guarded himself; his companions were only the zither and books, as if alone.

sentences.zh: 足不曆園庭，殆將十載。

translations.literal: His feet did not cross the garden courtyard for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: His feet did not cross the garden courtyard for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 子弟奉之若嚴君焉。

translations.literal: Younger and elder kin served him as if he were a stern lord.
translations.idiomatic: Younger and elder kin served him as if he were a stern lord.

sentences.zh: 其有過者，靖必下帷自責，於是長幼相率拜謝於庭，靖然後見之，勖以禮法。

translations.literal: When any had faults, Jing would always draw the curtain and blame himself; then young and old together would bow in apology in the courtyard, and only then would Jing see them and exhort them with ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: When any had faults, Jing would always draw the curtain and blame himself; then young and old together would bow in apology in the courtyard, and only then would Jing see them and exhort them with ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 鄉里亦慕而化之，或有不善者，皆曰：「唯恐柳德廣知也。」

translations.literal: The neighborhood also admired and was transformed; if any did wrong they would say: "We only fear that Liu Deguang will know".
translations.idiomatic: The neighborhood also admired and was transformed; if any did wrong they would say, "We only fear that Liu Deguang will know".

sentences.zh: 時論方之王烈。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion ranked him with Wang Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion ranked him with Wang Lie.

sentences.zh: 前後總管到官，皆親至靖家問疾，遂以為故事。

translations.literal: Former and later regional commanders, on taking office, all personally visited Jing's home to inquire after his health, and this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Former and later regional commanders, on taking office, all personally visited Jing's home to inquire after his health, and this became precedent.

sentences.zh: 秦王俊臨州，賚以几杖，並致衣物。

translations.literal: When Prince Jun of Qin came to the province, he bestowed an armrest and staff and also sent clothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jun of Qin came to the province, he bestowed an armrest and staff and also sent clothing.

sentences.zh: 靖唯受几杖，餘並固辭。

translations.literal: Jing accepted only the armrest and staff; the rest he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Jing accepted only the armrest and staff; the rest he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 其為當時所重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the weight in which he was held in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the weight in which he was held in his time.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，壽終。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he died at full years.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era he died at full years.

sentences.zh: 莊字思敬，少有器量，博覽墳籍，兼善辭令。

translations.literal: Zhuang, style name Sijing, from youth had capacity and measure, broadly read the classics, and was also skilled in elegant speech.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang, whose style name was Sijing, from youth had capacity and measure, broadly read the classics, and was also skilled in elegant speech.

sentences.zh: 濟陽蔡大寶有重名于江左，時為岳陽王蕭詧諮議，見莊，歎曰：「襄陽水鏡，復在於茲！」

translations.literal: Cai Dabao of Jiyang had heavy fame east of the Yangtze; at that time he was Consulting Advisor to the Prince of Yueyang Xiao Cha and, on seeing Zhuang, sighed: "The mirror of Xiangyang water is found here again"!
translations.idiomatic: Cai Dabao of Jiyang had heavy fame east of the Yangtze; at that time he was Consulting Advisor to the Prince of Yueyang Xiao Cha and, on seeing Zhuang, sighed, "The mirror of Xiangyang water is found here again"!

sentences.zh: 大寶遂以其女妻之。

translations.literal: Dabao thereupon gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Dabao thereupon gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 俄而察辟為參軍。

translations.literal: Soon Cha summoned him as Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Cha summoned him as Adjutant.

sentences.zh: 及詧稱帝，累遷鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: When Cha declared himself emperor, Zhuang was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha declared himself emperor, Zhuang was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝輔政，蕭巋令莊奉書入關。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as regent, Xiao Kui had Zhuang carry a letter into the pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as regent, Xiao Kui had Zhuang carry a letter into the pass.

sentences.zh: 時三方構難，文帝懼巋有異志，及莊還，謂曰：「孤昔以開府從役江陵，深蒙梁主殊眷。

translations.literal: At that time the three regions were embroiled in conflict; Emperor Wen feared Kui had a different intent, and when Zhuang returned he said to him: "I once followed the open headquarters in service at Jiangling and deeply received the Liang ruler's special favor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the three regions were embroiled in conflict; Emperor Wen feared Kui had a different intent, and when Zhuang returned he said to him, "I once followed the open headquarters in service at Jiangling and deeply received the Liang ruler's special favor.

sentences.zh: 今主幼時艱，猥蒙顧托。

translations.literal: Now the ruler is young and the times are hard; I have undeservedly received his trust as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Now the ruler is young and the times are hard; I have undeservedly received his trust as regent.

sentences.zh: 梁主弈業重光，委誠朝廷，而今已後，方見松筠之節。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler's imperial enterprise shines anew; he has entrusted his loyalty to the court, and from now on we shall see the steadfastness of pine and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler's imperial enterprise shines anew; he has entrusted his loyalty to the court, and from now on we shall see the steadfastness of pine and bamboo.

sentences.zh: 君還申孤此意于梁主也。」

translations.literal: When you return, convey this intent of mine to the Liang ruler".
translations.idiomatic: When you return, convey this intent of mine to the Liang ruler".

sentences.zh: 遂執莊手而別。

translations.literal: He then took Zhuang's hand in parting.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Zhuang's hand in parting.

sentences.zh: 時梁之將帥咸請與尉遲迥連衡，進可盡節于周氏，退可席捲山南，唯巋疑不可。

translations.literal: At that time Liang's generals all asked to ally with Wei Chijiong—advancing, they could exhaust their loyalty to the house of Zhou; retreating, they could sweep up the lands south of the mountains—only Kui doubted and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liang's generals all asked to ally with Wei Chijiong—advancing, they could exhaust their loyalty to the house of Zhou; retreating, they could sweep up the lands south of the mountains—only Kui doubted and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 會莊至自長安，申文帝結托之意，遂言於巋曰：「今尉遲迥雖曰舊將，昏耄已甚。

translations.literal: When Zhuang arrived from Chang'an and conveyed Emperor Wen's intent of entrusted alliance, he then said to Kui: "Now Wei Chijiong, though called an old general, is already deeply senile.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang arrived from Chang'an and conveyed Emperor Wen's intent of entrusted alliance, he then said to Kui, "Now Wei Chijiong, though called an old general, is already deeply senile.

sentences.zh: 消難、王謙常人之下者，非有匡合之才。

translations.literal: Xiao Nan and Wang Qian are men below the common run and lack the talent to restore unity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Nan and Wang Qian are men below the common run and lack the talent to restore unity.

sentences.zh: 況山東、庸蜀從化日近，周室之恩未洽於朝廷。

translations.literal: Moreover, east of the mountains and in Yong-Shu submission draws nearer day by day, and Zhou's grace has not yet reached the court.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, east of the mountains and in Yong-Shu submission draws nearer day by day, and Zhou's grace has not yet reached the court.

sentences.zh: 臣料之，迥等終當覆滅，隨公必私周國，未若保境息人，以觀其變。」

translations.literal: By my estimate, Chijiong and the others will in the end be overthrown; Duke Sui will surely seize Zhou for himself—it is better to guard the borders and give the people rest, and watch how things change".
translations.idiomatic: By my estimate, Chijiong and the others will in the end be overthrown; Duke Sui will surely seize Zhou for himself—it is better to guard the borders and give the people rest, and watch how things change".

sentences.zh: 巋深以為然。

translations.literal: Kui deeply thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: Kui deeply thought this right.

sentences.zh: 未幾，消難奔陳，迥及謙相次就戮。

translations.literal: Before long Xiao Nan fled to Chen, and Chijiong and Qian were executed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiao Nan fled to Chen, and Chijiong and Qian were executed in succession.

sentences.zh: 巋謂莊曰：「近若從眾言，社稷已不守矣。」

translations.literal: Kui said to Zhuang: "Had I lately followed the crowd's advice, the altars would already have been lost".
translations.idiomatic: Kui said to Zhuang, "Had I lately followed the crowd's advice, the altars would already have been lost".

sentences.zh: 文帝踐祚，莊又入朝，帝深慰勉之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Zhuang again entered court, and the Emperor deeply comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Zhuang again entered court, and the Emperor deeply comforted and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 及為晉王廣納妃于梁，莊因是往來四五反，前後賜物數千段。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin Guang took a consort from Liang, Zhuang therefore went back and forth four or five times and was repeatedly given gifts numbering thousands of lengths.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin Guang took a consort from Liang, Zhuang therefore went back and forth four or five times and was repeatedly given gifts numbering thousands of lengths.

sentences.zh: 梁國廢，授開府儀同三司，除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Liang state was abolished, he was appointed Grand Master with the third rank of ceremonial parity and made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Presentation of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang state was abolished, he was appointed Grand Master with the third rank of ceremonial parity and made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Presentation of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 莊明習舊章，雅達政事，凡所駁正，帝莫不稱善。

translations.literal: Zhuang clearly knew old regulations and was elegantly versed in administration; whatever he corrected, the Emperor always praised as good.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang clearly knew old regulations and was elegantly versed in administration; whatever he corrected, the Emperor always praised as good.

sentences.zh: 蘇威為納言，重莊器識，常奏帝云：「江南人有學業者，多不習世務；

translations.literal: Su Wei as Chief Speaker valued Zhuang's capacity and insight and often memorialized the Emperor, saying: "Among men of the south with learning, many do not practice worldly affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei as Chief Speaker valued Zhuang's capacity and insight and often memorialized the Emperor, saying, "Among men of the south with learning, many do not practice worldly affairs;

sentences.zh: 習世務者，又無學業。

translations.literal: those who practice worldly affairs have no learning.
translations.idiomatic: those who practice worldly affairs have no learning.

sentences.zh: 能兼之者，不過柳莊。」

translations.literal: Those who combine both are no more than Liu Zhuang".
translations.idiomatic: Those who combine both are no more than Liu Zhuang".

sentences.zh: 高熲亦與莊甚厚。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong was also very close to Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong was also very close to Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 莊與陳茂同官，不能降意。

translations.literal: Zhuang and Chen Mao held the same office but could not lower his will.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang and Chen Mao held the same office but could not lower his will.

sentences.zh: 茂見上及朝臣多屬意于莊，心每不平。

translations.literal: Mao saw that the Emperor and court ministers mostly favored Zhuang, and in his heart he was always displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Mao saw that the Emperor and court ministers mostly favored Zhuang, and in his heart he was always displeased.

sentences.zh: 帝與茂有舊，譖訴頗行。

translations.literal: The Emperor had old ties with Mao, and slander and complaints often took effect.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had old ties with Mao, and slander and complaints often took effect.

sentences.zh: 尚書省嘗奏犯罪人，依法合流，而上處以大辟。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing once memorialized a criminal; by law he should be banished, but the Emperor sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing once memorialized a criminal; by law he should be banished, but the Emperor sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 莊據法執之，帝不從，由是忤旨。

translations.literal: Zhuang held to the law and resisted; the Emperor would not follow, and thereby Zhuang offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang held to the law and resisted; the Emperor would not follow, and thereby Zhuang offended the imperial will.
